# Experiment Design: Distributional Similarity of Forward-Model Sampled Trajectories to Ground-Truth MD on Key Collective Variables

*Design-only document. No experiment has been run and no numerical results are reported. All values that are design choices (e.g., k = 3 TICA components, τ = 5 ps, α = 0.05) are stated as choices with rationale, not as facts from the source. The design is parameterised over the sequence S, the force field FF, and the forward simulation model M_fwd, so it reads correctly for any concrete instantiation.*

---

## 1. Objective and Hypothesis

**Objective.** Determine whether trajectories sampled from the forward simulation model M_fwd exhibit distributional similarity to ground-truth all-atom MD trajectories of a tetrapeptide, evaluated across three families of collective variables (CVs): backbone torsions, sidechain torsions, and the top TICA components.

**Framing.** This is a family of per-CV two-sample distributional tests plus an aggregate conclusion, not a single global claim. For each CV c we compare the marginal distribution P_MD(c) (ground truth) against P_fwd(c) (forward model).

**Hypotheses.**
- **H0 (per CV c):** P_MD(c) = P_fwd(c) — the forward model is distributionally indistinguishable from MD on c.
- **H1 (per CV c):** P_MD(c) ≠ P_fwd(c).
- **Aggregate H0:** P_MD(c) = P_fwd(c) for all CVs c in the family. The aggregate conclusion is derived from the corrected (FDR) test outcomes, not from any single CV.

**Decision rule summary.** The forward model is judged "distributionally similar" if, after Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control at α = 0.05 across the full CV family, **no CV family is rejected** (i.e., no backbone torsion, no sidechain torsion, and no top TICA component has an FDR-significant difference). If any CV is rejected, we report which CVs and which family, and the model is judged "not fully similar" with the specific deviations enumerated.

---

## 2. System Definition (parameterised over S, FF, M_fwd)

The design is deliberately agnostic to source-specific details and is written against three parameters:

- **S** — a tetrapeptide sequence (four residues, unspecified). The concrete sequence is a parameter to be supplied at instantiation. All CV counts and the ω treatment are functions of S.
- **FF** — the force field used to generate the ground-truth MD (unspecified). The ω treatment and torsion conventions are functions of FF.
- **M_fwd** — the forward simulation model whose sampled trajectories are being evaluated (identity unspecified: it may be a learned generative model, a Markov state model, or a physics-based / coarse-grained engine). The sampling protocol, autocorrelation handling, and negative-control definition are **conditional on M_fwd** (see §5 and the decision table in §6.4).

**Ground-truth data.** N_MD all-atom MD frames of S under FF, at a defined frame spacing Δt (to be supplied). This is the reference distribution.

**Forward data.** N_fwd frames sampled from M_fwd for the same system S. The relationship between N_fwd and N_MD, and whether M_fwd samples are i.i.d. or serially correlated, is parameterised by M_fwd.

**General CV rules (depend on S and FF).**
- **ω (peptide-bond torsion):** excluded from the CV set if FF constrains the peptide bond (the common case for standard all-atom protein force fields, where ω ≈ 180° is rigid). If FF treats ω as a free degree of freedom, ω is included per residue. State the actual treatment for the instantiated FF in the report header.
- **χ1:** present for every residue with a rotamer-bearing side chain (excluded for Gly, and for Ala which has no χ1). 
- **χ2:** present only for residues with the appropriate sidechain topology — e.g., Arg, Gln, Glu, Lys, Phe, Tyr, Trp (and His in many conventions). Absent otherwise.
- Residue indexing is 1..4 along the tetrapeptide backbone.

---

## 3. Collective Variables

### 3.1 Backbone torsions
Per residue i = 1..4: φ_i and ψ_i. (ω_i only if FF leaves it free, per §2.) These are the primary univariate CVs and are also the TICA input features (§3.3).

### 3.2 Sidechain torsions
χ1_i for all rotamer-bearing residues; χ2_i for residues with the topology listed in §2. The exact set is determined by S at instantiation.

### 3.3 TICA components
- **Feature set (design choice, per binding decision #2):** the TICA input is the set of **backbone torsions (φ_i, ψ_i) and sidechain torsions (χ1_i, χ2_i where defined)** evaluated per frame. Rationale: this is the most physically interpretable choice for a small tetrapeptide and keeps the TICA components directly comparable to the torsion CVs they summarise. *Alternative (noted, not primary):* if numerical stability at four-residue scale is a concern, a richer feature set (e.g., CA–CA or backbone-atom displacement distances) may be substituted; this is recorded as a fallback, not the default.
- **Lag time τ (design choice, per binding decision #3):** a **small fixed lag, τ = 5 ps** (or 10 ps if the assumed sampling timescale makes 5 ps an outlier), chosen to be short relative to the slowest expected tetrapeptide relaxation yet long enough to decorrelate fast local noise. **No automatic AR1-based lag selection is used as the primary method** — it is fragile at the short trajectory lengths typical of tetrapeptides. A **sensitivity sweep over τ ∈ {1, 5, 10, 20, 50} ps** is reported in a supplementary table showing the top TICA components and the per-CV test outcomes at each τ.
- **Basis (design choice, per binding decision #1):** the TICA model (covariance eigen-decomposition of the lagged feature dynamics) is **fit on the ground-truth MD trajectory only**, and **both** the MD frames and the M_fwd sampled frames are **projected into this shared MD-derived basis**. Rationale: the scientific question is whether M_fwd reproduces the *slow collective motions of the real system*, so "slow" is defined by the MD reference frame. Fitting a separate TICA per dataset would define two different linear subspaces and conflate "is the forward model capturing MD slow modes" with "do the two datasets have similar intrinsic slow modes."
- **Number of components k (design choice):** **k = 3** by default, selected as the smallest k capturing the dominant share of the slow-modes variance, operationalised as the largest gap in the TICA eigenvalue spectrum. A sensitivity sweep over **k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5}** is reported so the conclusion is not an artefact of this choice.

The TICA CVs are TICA_1, TICA_2, TICA_3 (and TICA_4, TICA_5 in the k-sweep), each a 1-D coordinate in the shared MD basis.

---

## 4. Similarity Metrics and Statistical Tests

For each CV we report a distribution-free test statistic plus corroborating distance/overlap measures. No kernel-bandwidth tuning is required for the primary decision metrics.

### 4.1 Univariate CVs (each torsion, each TICA coordinate)
- **Primary test — two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS).** Non-parametric, distribution-free, directly tests the null that the two samples come from the same distribution; the test statistic D is the sup-norm CDF difference and yields a p-value.
- **2-Wasserstein distance (1-D Earth Mover's Distance).** Sensitive to the *magnitude* of distributional shift in the CV's native units (deg for torsions, TICA units for components), complementing KS which is shape/orientation-focused.
- **Histogram L1 distance.** A robust, interpretable aggregate over binned densities; guards against KS's sensitivity to single-frame outliers.

### 4.2 Bivariate CVs (φ_i–ψ_i pairs; TICA_a–TICA_b pairs)
- **Energy distance.** A 2-sample distance that is zero iff the two joint distributions are equal and requires no bandwidth/kernel choice (a kernel-free analogue to MMD). Primary bivariate decision metric.
- **Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) with an RBF kernel (optional corroboration).** Reported alongside energy distance; kernel width set by the median-heuristic to keep it reproducible.

### 4.3 Overlap (descriptive, not a formal test)
- **Histogram-based overlap coefficient / mutual-information overlap** between P_MD(c) and P_fwd(c), reported as a descriptive summary of how much the two distributions share, not used for the accept/reject decision.

### 4.4 Test family and multiplicity correction (per binding decision #6)
For a tetrapeptide with sequence S, the **univariate test family** is:
{ φ1, ψ1, φ2, ψ2, φ3, ψ3, φ4, ψ4, χ1(1), χ1(2), χ1(3), χ1(4), χ2(residues where defined), TICA_1, TICA_2, TICA_3 }.
(The exact χ entries and any ω entries are filled in from S and FF at instantiation.)

- **Correction:** **Benjamini–Hochberg FDR at α = 0.05** across this family.
- **Reporting:** a **summary table** listing, for each CV: the raw p-value (from KS, primary) and the BH-adjusted q-value, plus the corroborating Wasserstein, L1, and (where applicable) energy-distance values. The accept/reject decision uses the q-value threshold.
- Bivariate (φ–ψ, TICA–TICA) energy-distance tests are reported as a secondary, non-gated family; if they are to be gated they would be added to the FDR family and the correction recomputed — the primary decision is driven by the univariate family above.

---

## 5. Controls and Null Models

### 5.1 Positive control (metric calibration)
- **Ground-truth MD vs. an independent ground-truth MD replica** of the same system S/FF. Expected outcome: low KS D, low energy distance, no FDR-significant differences. This establishes the metric's null behaviour and confirms that the pipeline does not manufacture false positives from sampling noise alone. If the positive control shows spurious "differences," the trajectory length / block size is insufficient and must be increased before trusting the primary comparison.

### 5.2 Negative control (power check, per binding decision #7)
Concrete, in priority order:
1. **Preferred:** sample the same number of frames from an **untrained or randomly initialised version of M_fwd** (if such a variant exists for the given M_fwd).
2. **Fallback:** sample from the MD trajectory of a **different tetrapeptide sequence** (e.g., S with one residue swapped to a chemically distinct amino acid).
3. **Last resort:** a **label-permutation test on the MD data itself** (shuffle frame labels between two MD halves) as the null.
Expected outcome: **clear separation** — large KS statistic, large energy distance, FDR-significant differences — confirming the tests have power to detect a real distributional mismatch. If the negative control does *not* separate, the tests lack power and the "similar" verdict for M_fwd is not trustworthy.

### 5.3 Permutation / bootstrap nulls
- **Block bootstrap** (see §6.5) to obtain confidence intervals for each distance, accounting for MD autocorrelation.
- **Label permutation** (as in the last-resort negative control) to double-check that the observed M_fwd-vs-MD separation is not an artifact.

---

## 6. Analysis Pipeline (raw frames → summary statistics)

### 6.1 Preprocessing
1. Load frames with an MD library (MDAnalysis or MDTraj). Ground truth: N_MD frames; forward: N_fwd frames.
2. Strip solvent/ions; unwrap coordinates; confirm the same atom mapping / residue numbering for S across both datasets.
3. Verify frame spacing Δt is consistent (or document resampling to a common Δt for the MD side if needed).

### 6.2 Torsion computation
4. Compute per-frame backbone φ_i, ψ_i (and ω_i if free) and sidechain χ1_i, χ2_i for each frame, using FF-consistent dihedral definitions. Output: per-residue, per-CV time series.

### 6.3 TICA
5. Assemble the feature matrix from the §3.3 torsion feature set for the **MD** trajectory.
6. Fit TICA at the chosen lag τ (primary τ = 5 ps) on MD only; record eigenvalues and the top-k eigenvectors (k = 3 default).
7. **Project both** the MD frames and the M_fwd frames into the shared MD-derived TICA basis → TICA_1..TICA_k per frame for each dataset.
8. Repeat steps 5–7 for the τ-sweep {1,5,10,20,50} ps and the k-sweep {1,2,3,5} for the supplementary tables.

### 6.4 Autocorrelation handling (conditional on M_fwd, per binding decision #4)
The block-bootstrap strategy depends on the autocorrelation structure of the forward model. **Decision table:**

| M_fwd type | Sample autocorrelation | Block bootstrap applied to |
|---|---|---|
| Learned generative model (diffusion, flow, score-based) | i.i.d. by construction | **MD side only** (forward frames treated as independent) |
| Markov state model | Serially correlated | **Both sides** |
| Physics-based / coarse-grained engine | Serially correlated | **Both sides** |

(If M_fwd is a learned generative model but produces trajectories that are internally correlated by construction — e.g., an autoregressive dynamics model — treat it as serially correlated and apply block bootstrap to both sides; this is the conservative default when in doubt.)

### 6.5 Block bootstrap for uncertainty
9. For each dataset, partition the frame series into **blocks** whose length exceeds the integrated autocorrelation time (estimated from the series' lagged autocorrelation; a minimum sensible block length is enforced for short trajectories).
10. Resample blocks with replacement B times (e.g., B = 1000) to build bootstrap distributions of each distance (Wasserstein, L1, energy distance) and of the KS statistic; derive confidence intervals and p-values.
11. This step is what makes the two-sample inference valid given MD's strong frame-to-frame autocorrelation.

### 6.6 Statistics and aggregation
12. For each CV in the §4.4 family, compute the primary KS p-value and the corroborating distances from the (block-bootstrap-resampled) samples.
13. Apply BH FDR at α = 0.05 → q-values.
14. Produce the summary table (CV, raw p, q, Wasserstein, L1, energy distance where applicable, pass/fail).
15. Run the positive and negative controls (§5) through the identical pipeline and report their outcomes.

---

## 7. Decision Criteria

- **"Distributionally similar":** after BH FDR at α = 0.05 across the univariate family, **no CV is rejected** (all q ≥ 0.05), AND the positive control shows no spurious rejections, AND the negative control shows clear separation (power confirmed).
- **"Not similar":** one or more CVs have q < 0.05. Report exactly which CVs and which family (backbone / sidechain / TICA) deviate, with the magnitude from the corroborating distances.
- **Aggregate conclusion:** reported as the count and identity of FDR-significant CVs, grouped by family, plus the pass/fail status of both controls. A "similar" verdict is issued only when all three conditions above hold; otherwise the verdict is "not fully similar" with the specific deviations enumerated.
- **Robustness gate:** the conclusion is stated to hold (or not) across the τ-sweep and k-sweep; if the verdict flips across the sweep, the design reports the sensitivity rather than a single point estimate.

---

## 8. Feasibility Assessment

- **Compute:** tetrapeptide all-atom systems are small (~100–200 heavy atoms). Computing per-frame torsions and a TICA over 10^5–10^7 frames is **computationally trivial** on the available **224-CPU** budget — expected to run in seconds to minutes per (τ, k) configuration, and the full sweep is still well within budget. No GPU is required (none is present).
- **Software requirements:** NumPy, SciPy, an MD library (MDAnalysis or MDTraj), and scikit-learn (for TICA / MMD). 
- **Sandbox limitation (stated explicitly):** the current sandbox has **none of these packages installed** (NumPy, SciPy, MDAnalysis/MDTraj, scikit-learn all absent) and **no network access**, so the pipeline **cannot be executed here** without a **pre-provisioned environment with offline wheels** (or a preinstalled conda/pip environment). 
- **Deliverability:** the design is fully deliverable as a document regardless; given a concrete (S, FF, M_fwd, trajectory files, Δt) and an offline-capable environment, a reader can execute it end-to-end. No experiment has been run and no results are claimed.

---

## 9. Assumptions and Sensitivity

Each item is a design assumption **not confirmed by the source**, with a one-sentence statement of what would change if it were wrong.

1. **Identity/nature of M_fwd** (learned generative vs. Markov state model vs. physics/coarse-grained engine) is unspecified. *If wrong:* the autocorrelation handling and negative-control definition change — the §6.4 decision table exists precisely to make the design agnostic, so the impact is confined to selecting the correct row.
2. **Tetrapeptide sequence S** is unspecified. *If wrong/different:* the exact CV set (which χ1/χ2 exist, residue count) changes, but the design reads correctly for any S via the §2 general rules.
3. **Force field FF** for ground truth is unspecified. *If wrong:* the ω treatment (include/exclude) and torsion conventions may change; the design handles this by making ω conditional on FF in §2.
4. **Trajectory length and replica count** (both MD and forward) are unspecified. *If wrong/too short:* statistical power drops and TICA can become unstable — the positive/negative controls and block-bootstrap CIs are the built-in guards, and the design would require longer trajectories if the positive control shows spurious rejections.
5. **TICA lag τ = 5 ps** is a design choice. *If the true slow timescale differs:* the identified slow modes shift; the τ-sweep {1,5,10,20,50} ps exposes this and the robustness gate (§7) reports whether the verdict is τ-dependent.
6. **TICA component count k = 3** is a design choice. *If the system's slow dynamics are concentrated in fewer or more modes:* the compared subspace changes; the k-sweep {1,2,3,5} reports sensitivity.
7. **TICA basis fit on MD and projected onto both datasets** is a design choice. *If the intent were instead per-dataset intrinsic comparison:* the shared-basis choice would be the wrong frame, but this was explicitly settled (binding decision #1) to match the "reproduce MD slow motions" question.
8. **"Distributional similarity" interpreted as per-CV marginals + pairwise joints, not full path-level.** *If path-level similarity were intended:* the design would need a time-series distance (e.g., DTW) and a different null; as written it answers the marginal/joint reading of "across key CVs."

---

## 10. Limitations

- **Marginal/joint focus:** the design compares distributions of individual CVs and pairwise joints, not full trajectory paths or higher-order joint structure; two models could pass every tested CV yet differ in untested correlations.
- **TICA basis dependence:** TICA components are defined by the MD fit; differences in TICA coordinates are meaningful only within the shared MD basis and are not invariant to feature-set or lag choice (hence the sweeps).
- **Power limited by trajectory length:** at short tetrapeptide trajectory lengths, block-bootstrap CIs are wide and FDR may under-detect subtle shifts; the negative control is the primary safeguard, and a null negative control invalidates a "similar" verdict.
- **Torsion-based TICA features:** using torsions as TICA input (a design choice for interpretability) may be less stable than a richer geometric feature set for very small systems; the CA–CA alternative is documented but not primary.
- **Environment:** the design cannot be executed in the current sandbox (missing packages, no network); feasibility is a statement about a properly provisioned offline environment, not a demonstration.
- **No execution / no results:** this is a design only; no experiment has been run and no empirical outcome is asserted.

# Final Experiment Design: Distributional Similarity of Forward-Model-Sampled Trajectories vs Ground-Truth MD (Tetrapeptide System)

*Design-only document. No experiment has been run; this specifies a reproducible protocol, not results.*

## 1. Objective

Determine whether trajectories sampled from the forward simulation model are distributionally similar to ground-truth all-atom MD trajectories of the same tetrapeptide, quantified across three collective-variable (CV) families: (a) backbone torsions (φ, ψ), (b) sidechain torsions (χ1, χ2 where defined), and (c) top TICA components. The design produces a per-CV-family verdict (similar / not similar / mixed) with uncertainty quantification, benchmarked against a same-distribution (MD-vs-MD) null rather than an arbitrary threshold.

## 2. System & Data Sources

- **System:** tetrapeptide in all-atom MD (per researcher-provided context). *Assumed sequence: a mixed-composition tetrapeptide containing at least one residue with a defined χ1 (e.g., a standard 4-residue sequence such as Ala-X-Y-Z); the actual sequence must be read from the paper's setup (topics setup_2/13/14) before execution, since the sidechain CV set depends on it.*
- **Forward model:** generative model trained on MD data that produces trajectories from an initial structure (identity/architecture to be confirmed from the source). At execution time: obtain the released/final checkpoint.
- **Reference (ground-truth) MD:** the paper's all-atom MD trajectories for the same tetrapeptide, same force field, temperature, and initial condition as used in the model's training/evaluation protocol. Use the full available reference set; subsample to N_r = 100 only for the MD-vs-MD control to keep computation symmetric.
- **Train/eval relationship:** record whether the evaluation reference set overlaps the model's training data; if the paper defines a held-out evaluation MD set, use it; otherwise evaluate on the full reference set and flag the overfitting risk in reporting (see Controls C6).
- **Workspace note:** `/workspace` currently contains only `task.json` — no data, checkpoints, or trajectories. All artifacts above must be sourced at execution time; the design is a self-contained blueprint.

## 3. Collective Variables

With only 4 residues, all per-residue CVs are reported as **compact tables** (one row per residue), not heatmaps.

1. **Backbone torsions:** per-residue φ and ψ (residues with both defined; for a tetrapeptide typically residues 2–3 fully, residue 1 ψ and residue 4 φ depending on terminal handling — state the terminal convention explicitly in the run log). Pooled (all residues, all frames) distributions also reported.
2. **Sidechain torsions:** χ1 for residues with a defined χ1; χ2 where defined (e.g., residues with ≥2 sidechain rotatable bonds). The exact set is determined by the confirmed sequence (e.g., if the tetrapeptide contains Gly, no sidechain torsions for that residue). Group by residue type for the aggregate table.
3. **TICA components:** top-k TICA components, **k = 2 default, sweep over k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5}**. TICA is fitted **on the reference MD set only** (fixed lag time from the paper's protocol, else 10 ps) and applied unchanged to sampled trajectories. The lag-correlation eigenvalue spectrum is reported; the final k is chosen as the largest value whose eigenvalues are meaningfully separated from the near-unity floor (with k = 2 as the fallback default, since a tetrapeptide has few conformational degrees of freedom and k = 5 may be over-interpretive).
4. **Torsion representation:** all angles computed in [−180°, 180°) and treated as circular in 1D metrics (circular statistics / wrapped differences); 2D (φ,ψ) pairs treated on the torus.

## 4. Similarity Metrics (multi-level suite)

1. **Per-dimension (1D, per CV):**
   - Energy distance (E-statistic) — primary, nonparametric, no bandwidth choice.
   - MMD with RBF kernel, median-heuristic bandwidth.
   - KDE overlap coefficient (integrated min-density) and two-sample KS p-value (secondary).
   - Reported per-residue (compact table: residue, CV, MMD, energy distance, p-value, bootstrap 95% CI) and pooled across residues.
2. **2D:**
   - Per-residue (φ, ψ) Ramachandran space: energy distance and MMD on 2D points; 2D KDE overlay plots (sample vs reference) for each residue.
   - 2D TICA (components 1 & 2): MMD / energy distance + KDE overlay.
3. **Multivariate:** MMD on the full k-dimensional TICA vector (k = 2 default; repeated for the sweep).
4. **Cheap sanity checks:** mean and covariance of each CV group; Mahalanobis distance between sample and reference Gaussians (per CV family) — reported as a quick consistency check, not the primary statistic.
5. **Inference on metrics:** nonparametric bootstrap (10,000 resamples) CIs for all primary distances; two-sample permutation p-values for energy distance where computationally trivial.

## 5. Controls

- **C1 — MD-vs-MD split baseline (primary null):** split the reference MD into two halves; compute the full metric suite between them. This is the expected distance for two samples from the *same* distribution. **Decision rule:** a CV family is "distributionally similar" if the sample-vs-reference distance falls within the 95th percentile of the MD-vs-MD null distribution (bootstrap over splits); "borderline" if within the 99th; otherwise "dissimilar."
- **C2 — Negative control:** compare the forward-model samples against MD trajectories from a *different* tetrapeptide/system or a different condition (e.g., different temperature or initial structure) if available in the paper; if no second system exists, use the same system's MD at a far time offset or a different initial condition. The distance must be clearly *larger* than the C1 null, confirming metric sensitivity.
- **C3 — Permutation control:** permute CV identity (e.g., compare sample TICA component 1 against reference component 2; rotate the residue assignment of torsions). The metric suite must detect the mismatch (distance > null), confirming the metrics are not insensitive to the specific comparison.
- **C4 — TICA dimensionality control:** repeat all TICA-based metrics for k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5}; report the eigenvalue spectrum; conclusions must be stable across k (or the k-sensitivity itself reported as a finding).
- **C5 — Time/length control:** compute CV distances as a function of sampled time (or trajectory length) to detect drift away from the MD distribution over the generation horizon. This also handles the case where initial conditions are not shared (see Assumptions).
- **C6 — Train/reference split control:** if a held-out evaluation MD set exists, use it; if the evaluation set overlaps training data, run the comparison on both the full reference and (if available) a disjoint subset, and report both, flagging potential overfitting-inflated similarity.
- **C7 — Bandwidth/KDE sensitivity (secondary):** vary the RBF bandwidth by ×/÷2 and KDE bandwidth selection method to confirm MMD/overlap conclusions are not artifact-driven.

## 6. Analysis & Reporting Plan

1. **Data preparation:** extract per-residue φ/ψ and χ torsions from all frames of both sets (MDAnalysis-style dihedral calculation); fit TICA on reference only; project both sets.
2. **Primary tables:** one compact table per CV family — per-residue rows (residue, CV, sample MMD ± CI, reference-null MMD, energy distance, p-value, verdict vs C1 null) plus a pooled row.
3. **Primary plots:** per-residue Ramachandran 2D KDE overlays (sample vs reference); 2D TICA KDE overlays; TICA eigenvalue spectrum with chosen k marked; time-resolved distance curves (C5).
4. **Verdict structure:** per-family similarity verdict (backbone torsions / sidechain torsions / TICA) against the C1 null with the stated decision rule; overall conclusion stated as agreement or deviation, with the largest per-residue deviations named.
5. **Reproducibility:** fixed random seeds for sampling, bootstrapping, and any model stochasticity; versioned script that takes (model checkpoint, reference MD set, sample set) as inputs and emits the tables/plots; full run log including sequence, force field, TICA lag, k choice, and N values.

## 7. Feasibility

- **Compute:** CPU-only (224 cores available, no GPU). For a tetrapeptide, generating **N_s = 100 sampled trajectories is very feasible on CPU** even if the model is a diffusion model (small system, short trajectories); no pilot-size reduction is required, though a 10-trajectory smoke test is still run to validate the pipeline before the full batch.
- **CV extraction & TICA:** trivial for tetrapeptide scale (≤4 torsion residues, small lag-correlation matrix); TICA sweep over k ∈ {1,2,3,5} is negligible cost.
- **Metrics:** energy distance is O(n log n) with n = frames × residues — trivial; MMD and 10,000-resample bootstraps across ~10–20 CVs are minutes-to-an-hour on CPU.
- **Dependencies:** numpy/scipy (core), MDAnalysis or equivalent for torsion extraction, scikit-learn (MMD convenience). Not preinstalled in this workspace; the execution environment must have them or vendored wheels (network is disabled here, so the design specifies pinned requirements.txt as part of the deliverable).
- **Bottleneck risk:** only model inference for 100 trajectories; mitigated by the smoke test and, if needed, parallel generation across CPU cores.

## 8. Explicit Assumptions

1. **Tetrapeptide sequence is unknown from the brief** — assumed to be a standard 4-residue sequence containing at least one χ1-bearing residue; the actual sequence (from the paper's setup) fixes the sidechain CV table. If it is e.g. poly-Ala or contains Gly, the sidechain section shrinks accordingly but the design is unchanged.
2. **Forward model identity/architecture** — assumed to be a generative model trained on the paper's MD data that generates all-atom trajectories from an initial structure; exact architecture and generation protocol (diffusion vs autoregressive, number of generator steps, horizon) to be confirmed from topics setup_2/setup_13/setup_14 (6 clarifying questions remain available if needed before execution).
3. **Initial-condition alignment** — assumed sampled trajectories start from the same initial structure(s) as the reference MD, making time-0 distributions comparable; if not, C5 (time-resolved) becomes the primary lens and all verdicts are stated relative to a common time origin.
4. **Sample size/length** — N_s = 100 sampled trajectories, N_r = 100 for the MD-vs-MD control; trajectory length matched to the paper's standard generation horizon / reference length.
5. **TICA** — default k = 2 with sweep {1, 2, 3, 5}; lag time from the paper's protocol, else 10 ps; fitted on reference only.
6. **Train/reference overlap** — unknown; C6 covers both cases.
7. **MD protocol** — reference MD assumed to be the paper's all-atom simulation (same force field/temperature/box) as used to train/evaluate the model.
8. **Negative-control availability** — assumed a second system/condition or at least a different initial condition exists; if nothing does, C2 falls back to time-offset comparison within the same MD (weaker, flagged as such).

No empirical results are claimed or implied by this document; it is the complete protocol to be executed later.

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design — Does MDGEN recover fast (torsion) dynamics missing from subsampled MD trajectories?

Design-only deliverable. No experiment was run; no results are reported. All "expected outcome" statements are explicitly labeled **hypotheses**.

## 1. Rationale
Subsampling an MD trajectory (keeping every N-th frame) discards the high-frequency content of the motion. A torsion angle oscillates at a characteristic frequency f0; if the subsampling interval N·dt approaches or exceeds the oscillation period, that fast motion is aliased away. The question is whether MDGEN, given only the subsampled frames, can regenerate the in-between frames such that the *derived* torsion angle again carries the correct high-frequency content. The design therefore: (a) picks a system with one clean, measurable torsion oscillator; (b) sweeps the subsampling factor across the Nyquist point of that oscillator so "recover" is a well-posed, bounded question; (c) uses the power spectrum of the torsion as the primary metric, because "recovering fast dynamics" is fundamentally about recovering high-frequency spectral power; and (d) compares against trivial interpolation to isolate genuine value-add. The single biggest scientific risk — that MDGEN is a forward-prediction model being used for gap-filling — is treated as an explicit limitation, not asserted away.

## 2. System and subsampling sweep
**Primary system (locked): 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), GAFF force field.** Chosen for a clean single torsion oscillator (central C–C dihedral, O–C–C–O), low barrier (~2–3 kcal/mol), and small size (18 atoms incl. H) enabling a long 2 fs reference trajectory cheaply.
**Secondary robustness check (not co-equal): alanine dipeptide, ff14sb** — a multi-torsion, coupled system, used only to test whether the primary-system conclusion generalizes.

- Native MD timestep dt = 2 fs. **2 fs low-pass limit: Nyquist f_N = 1/(2·dt) = 250 THz.** The ground truth cannot represent torsion motion above 250 THz, so every "recover" claim is scoped to f < 250 THz. This is a scope limitation, not a detail.
- **Fast-dynamics band (explicit):** defined self-calibratingly from the reference's own torsion PSD as [f0, min(5·f0, f_N)], where f0 is the dominant torsion oscillation frequency measured from the full 2 fs trajectory. For DME the central C–C torsion is a sub-THz-to-low-THz oscillator (f0 ≈ 5–10 THz, period ~100–200 fs), giving a concrete band ≈ 5–25 THz, capped at the 250 THz ceiling (the cap does not bind for DME). If the researcher's "100–500" figure was intended in a specific unit, it maps onto this operational band; the self-calibrating definition is primary and the numeric example is the DME instantiation.
- **Subsampling sweep (brackets the Nyquist point of f0 ≈ 5–10 THz):** N ∈ {5, 10, 20, 50}. Effective Nyquist = f_N/N: N=5 → 50 THz (recoverable), N=10 → 25 THz (recoverable), N=20 → 12.5 THz (near crossover), N=50 → 5 THz (below f0 → aliased/unrecoverable). This bracketing is the crux: it spans recoverable, borderline, and aliased regimes.
- **MDGEN conditioning protocol (locked, most defensible in-distribution form):** MDGEN is used in its native mode — predict the next frame at dt given a history window of K frames at dt spacing (forward prediction). We drive it sequentially: at each real subsampled anchor we (re)initialize/verify the history window, then generate the N−1 in-between frames one dt step at a time, feeding each generated frame back into the history window so subsequent steps see dt-spaced context. This keeps the model at its trained dt and history structure as much as possible.
  - **Ablation A (bidirectional gap-filling):** condition on both the left and right anchors (two-sided conditioning). More information, but more clearly an extrapolation from the trained forward objective — reported separately.
  - **Ablation B (no re-seed):** generate an entire gap from a single anchor without re-seeding, to isolate drift.
  - **Limitation (stated, not asserted):** no model card exists, so we cannot assert in-distributionness. Even the anchored-forward protocol carries a time-spacing extrapolation at anchor boundaries (the history gap is N·dt, not dt). This is an uncontrolled error source we acknowledge; we do not claim the protocol is in-distribution.
- **Baselines (value-add test, locked):** (a) linear interpolation in θ-space; (b) cubic spline in θ-space; (c) nearest-neighbor. MDGEN's value-add is measured against these, not against absolute error alone.

## 3. Metrics (derived-torsion pipeline spelled out)
**Derived-torsion pipeline (identical for GT, MDGEN output, and every baseline):**
1. Read atomic coordinates for each frame (GT at dt; MDGEN/baselines produce frames at dt).
2. Assign the DME central C–C dihedral on a fixed atom order (O–C–C–O); compute θ(t) per frame.
3. Wrap θ to [−180°,180°) for pointwise error; unwrap to a continuous time series for spectral/autocorrelation metrics.
4. Align every generated/baseline θ series to the GT dt timeline; metrics are computed on the derived θ, never on model output positions directly.

**Metrics:**
- **M1 — Per-frame torsion error:** RMSE and MAE (degrees) of generated θ(t) vs GT θ(t) at the (N−1) intermediate steps (anchor steps reported separately for sanity).
- **M2 — Power Spectral Density (PRIMARY):** Welch PSD of θ(t) for GT and each method. **Spectral recovery ratio** R = ∫_band PSD_gen(f)df / ∫_band PSD_gt(f)df over the fast band, plus band-limited cross-PSD coherence (gen vs GT). Reported per N.
- **M3 — Autocorrelation:** θ(t) autocorrelation decay, gen vs GT.
- **M4 — Dominant oscillation:** fundamental f0 and phase of generated vs GT (PSD peak / Hilbert transform); phase-locked accuracy.
- **M5 — Frame RMSD (Å):** position-space sanity control.

## 4. Controls
- **C1 — Nyquist bracketing:** the N sweep itself (recoverable → borderline → aliased).
- **C2 — Fully-aliased no-information control:** N=50 (eff Nyquist < f0) and/or a synthetic input with the fast band explicitly zeroed. **Expected result: failure** (R→0, high error). Validates that the metric can detect "no recovery."
- **C3 — Position-space control:** M5, to confirm any apparent recovery is in the nonlinear torsion coordinate, not trivial position interpolation.
- **C4 — Value-add baselines:** linear/cubic-spline/nearest-neighbor. If MDGEN does not beat cubic spline in the recoverable regime, the value-add claim fails.

## 5. Analysis plan
- **Per-N curves:** M1 (RMSE/MAE) vs N; M2 spectral recovery ratio R vs N; M4 f0/phase error vs N. One curve family per method (MDGEN primary, Ablation A, Ablation B, linear, cubic, nearest-neighbor).
- **Replicate count:** 3 independent MD reference replicas (different initial velocities / random seeds) × 3 independent MDGEN sampling seeds per (N, replica). Diffusion sampling is stochastic, so seeds are needed to separate generation noise from systematic error.
- **Uncertainty handling:** bootstrap 95% CI on RMSE and R (resampling over frames and over replicas); report MDGEN sampling-seed variance separately from systematic error.
- **Statistical test:** paired comparison of MDGEN vs cubic spline (paired t-test or Wilcoxon) over frames within each (N, replica).
- **Secondary system:** repeat the primary pipeline on alanine dipeptide (ff14sb) for a subset of N as a robustness check only.

## 6. Feasibility
- **MD (CPU-only):** DME (18 atoms). Recommend gas-phase or minimal solvation for speed. 1 ns at 2 fs = 500,000 frames; 3 replicas × 1 ns = 1.5M frames. Trivially feasible on CPU (224 cores available in this env; execution is external regardless).
- **Generation (GPU):** across the N sweep and replicas, on the order of ~10^6 generated frames (worst case N=5 generates 4/5 of frames). **Budget ≈ 1 A100-class GPU-day.** Noted as **external**: this environment has no GPU, so generation runs elsewhere.
- **Torsion/analysis:** pure Python/NumPy, CPU, minutes.
- **Total:** ~1 A100 GPU-day + modest CPU time, external execution.

## 7. Limitations
- **No model card:** MDGEN's training objective, dt, history length K, and conditioning interface are unverified. The anchored-forward protocol is best-effort in-distribution; extrapolation risk is real and unquantified. We do not assert in-distributionness.
- **2 fs low-pass:** GT cannot represent f > 250 THz; "recover" claims are confined to the resolvable band, and the very fastest modes (bond stretches, >250 THz) are out of scope.
- **Anchor-boundary time-spacing extrapolation:** the history gap of N·dt is an uncontrolled error source even in the primary protocol.
- **Single primary torsion:** DME is a clean single oscillator; positive DME results do not guarantee recovery for coupled multi-torsion systems (alanine dipeptide is a robustness check, not the main claim).
- **Derived nonlinear coordinate:** position-level fidelity (M5) and torsion fidelity can diverge; conclusions are about the torsion coordinate specifically.
- **Sampling stochasticity:** modest replicate count (3×3); CI reflects estimation, not a full error model.

## 8. Expected outcomes — HYPOTHESES (not findings)
- **H1:** In the recoverable regime (N=5,10), MDGEN recovers fast-band spectral power substantially (high R) with low torsion RMSE, comparable to or modestly better than cubic spline.
- **H2:** As N approaches the Nyquist crossover (N≈20), R degrades and RMSE rises.
- **H3:** In the aliased regime (N=50), recovery fails (R→0), matching the no-information control (validates the metric).
- **H4:** Bidirectional gap-filling (Ablation A) outperforms anchored-forward by using more information, but with higher extrapolation risk / lower reliability.
- **H5:** For a purely periodic fast oscillation, MDGEN may not beat trivial cubic interpolation — value-add may be small in the clean single-torsion case.

**Bottom line:** the experiment is well-posed because the Nyquist bracketing makes "recover" bounded and the PSD recovery ratio directly measures the fast-dynamics claim; the dominant open risk is the MDGEN objective mismatch, which is isolated via the conditioning protocol and reported as a limitation rather than assumed away.

**Есть только одно:** `/workspace/task.json` (8 КБ). Его содержимое:
- `question` — сам вопрос про MDGEN и быстрые динамики;
- `context` — «Design an experiment... Do not claim that an experiment was run» (design-only);
- `documents.track.md` — буквально: *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."*

**Чего нет (честно):**
- ❌ Никакого кода MDGEN — ни модели, ни весов, ни конфига, ни README.
- ❌ Никаких траекторий — ни subsampled, ни full-resolution/ground-truth, ни файлов .trr/.xtc/.lammpstrj/.dcd, ни координат.
- ❌ Никаких torsion angles, конфига системы, списков связей — т.е. из чего их считать, тоже нет.
- ❌ Никаких датасетов (поле `datasets` пустое), network disabled, GPU нет.

**Окружение:** Python 3.14.4, **numpy/scipy НЕ установлены** и поставить их нельзя (нет сети). CPU-аффинность 224 ядра — ресурс CPU есть, но библиотека только stdlib (`math`, `random`, `json` и т.п.).

Вывод: эксперимент можно строить только как **синтетический/симуляционный** — и это прямо подтверждается `track.md` (design-only, репо и compute не требуются).

## (2) Краткий approach (высокий уровень)

Вопрос «восстанавливает ли MDGEN быстрые dynamics» без реальной модели/данных проверяем через **контролируемый синтетический аналог**:

- **Ground truth:** синтетическая full-resolution «траектория» — torsion angles как сумма (а) медленной компоненты (низкочастотный дрейф/случайное блуждание) и (б) быстрых осцилляций с **точно известными** частотами/фазы/амплитудами (например, несколько затухающих синусоид в диапазоне, который subsampling должен «стереть» — частоты выше частоты Найквиста subsampled-сетки).
- **Input:** та же траектория, **subsampled** (каждые N шагов) — т.е. быстрые осцилляции aliased/удалены, остаются только медленная компонента + алиасинг-резидиуал.
- **Модель (MDGEN-заглушка):** небольшой генеративный блок, который по subsampled-последовательности предсказывает промежуточные шаги (например, простая RNN/MLP на чистом Python, или даже обучаемая линейная/нейросетевая интерполяция). Ключевое: модель не получает ground truth при инференсе.
- **Метрики (проекции на известную базу осцилляторов, без FFT):**
  1. Amplitude/phase recovery: корреляция и RMSE по каждой известной высокочастотной компоненте отдельно (проекция на sin/cos с известной частотой);
  2. Band-split: доля энергии в высокочастотном банде, восстановленная vs ground truth (energy ratio);
  3. Phase alignment (time lag до максимума кросс-корреляции) — «восстановил ли не только амплитуду, но и фазу/тайминг»;
  4. Sanity: точность на медленной компоненте (чтобы не было обмана «хорошо на медленной, плохо на быстрой»).
- **Controls:**
  1. **Trivial baseline — sinc-интерполяция / линейная интерполяция** (оптимальный реконструктор для band-limited сигнала). Если «модель» не бьёт или не приближает интерполяцию — восстановление частотной компоненты не заслуживает доверия;
  2. **Aliasing-контроль:** прогнать ту же модель на данных, где высокочастотная компонента *не* aliased (частота ниже Найквиста subsampled-сетки) — модель должна справляться лучше; различие между двумя режимами = вклад «реального восстановления» против «запомнения»;
  3. **Ablation по N** (степени subsampling) — кривая recovery vs N;
  4. **Null-контроль:** модель, обученная без высокочастотной компоненты в target — должна её не восстанавливать (проверка, что метрики не дают false positive от медленной компоненты);
  5. Leave-one-frequency-out: обучить на K−1 частотах, тестировать на K-й (обобщение vs запоминание).

Критерий ответа на вопрос: модель «точно восстанавливает» быстрые dynamics, если по метрикам 1–3 она статистически значимо превосходит null-контроль и не уступает интерполяционному baseline, и это сохраняется при росте N.

## (3) Consequential assumptions и uncertainties

**Assumptions (что мы предполагаем):**
1. **MDGEN — модель «subsampled → full» траекторий** (генеративная, предсказывает пропущенные шаги). Реальный MDGEN (если имеется в виду конкретная работа) может быть diffusion/autoregressive — архитектура не влияет на дизайн метрик, но влияет на реализацию заглушки; пока предполагаем generic sequence-to-sequence.
2. **Быстрый сигнал существует и является осцилляторным** (затухающие синусоиды по torsion angles — физически правдоподобно для малых молекул). Мы предполагаем, что это адекватная прокси реальных fast dynamics.
3. **Воспроизводимость ground truth допустима** как основа оценки (в реальной MD full-resolution run — и есть ground truth; в синтетике — аналитическая формула).
4. **Чистый Python stdlib достаточно** для реализации (метрики через проекции на известные частоты — без FFT/numpy).

**Uncertainties (что неясно и может сломать дизайн):**
1. **Что именно такое MDGEN** — нет ни кода, ни ссылки. Если это конкретная опубликованная модель с фиксированным API, заглушка может не отражать её поведение; эксперимент тогда отвечает на вопрос «может ли класс таких моделей восстанавливать быстрые dynamics», а не «восстанавливает ли именно этот MDGEN». *Это главный риск интерпретации.*
2. **Существует ли вообще не-алиасованный high-frequency сигнал, который можно восстановить** — для band-limited сигнала subsampling обратим (sinc), для реальных не-band-limited траекторий высокочастотная информация *безвозвратно потеряна* и никакая модель её «не восстановит», а лишь сгенерирует правдоподобную. Дизайн должен явно разделять эти два режима (aliased vs band-limited) — иначе ответ на вопрос неоднозначен.
3. **Runtime budget** — 224 ядра, но без numpy обучение даже мелкой RNN на чистом Python может быть медленным; бюджет на один полный прогон (обучение × несколько N × controls) не задан. Если бюджет мал, план В: заменить обучаемую модель на parametric family (подгонка затухающих осцилляторов) + интерполяционные baselines — это проверяет метрики и controls, но не «модель» как таковую.
4. **Масштаб** — сколько torsion angles, какая длина траектории, какая степень subsampling характерна для задачи — не задано; беру N ∈ {2..10}, 3–5 частот, длина ~10^4 шагов как разумные дефолты.

Следующий шаг после вашего одобрения: полный дизайн (exact синтетический генератор, формулы метрик, список controls с ожидаемым поведением каждого, протокол запуска на stdlib Python, критерии pass/fail и формат отчёта).

# Экспериментальный дизайн: «Восстанавливает ли MDGEN быстрые timestep dynamics, отсутствующие в subsampled траекториях?»

## 0. Framing и главный caveat (обязателен в отчёте)

В /workspace **нет кода, весов или данных MDGEN** (есть только task.json). Поэтому мы **не воспроизводим конкретную опубликованную архитектуру**, а конструируем **representative stand-in модели класса** «short-sequence autoregressive/generative interpolator» (вход — subsampled последовательность, выход — пропущенные шаги). Эксперимент отвечает на вопрос: *«может ли модель данного класса восстановить известные быстрые осцилляции»*, а не «делает ли именно этот MDGEN именно так». Это не ограничение дизайна, а его следствие из отсутствия кода; в отчёте формулируется как assumption с эксплицитным caveat. Никакие эксперименты не запускались — это design-only документ.

## 1. Rationale

Subsampling с фактором N (берём каждый N-й шаг) делает сетку с Nyquist-частотой f_Nyq(N) = 1/(2N) (циклов на full-resolution шаг). Отсюда два принципиально разных режима, которые **нельзя смешивать в одном протоколе**, иначе ответ на вопрос «восстанавливает ли» неоднозначен:

- **Arm A — band-limited (f < f_Nyq(N)):** сигнал теоретически восстанавливаем — subsampling обратим (sinc-интерполяция — оптимальный реконструктор). Прогноз: хорошая модель должна **превосходить** тривиальные интерполяторы и приближать sinc.
- **Arm B — aliased (f > f_Nyq(N)):** высокочастотная информация **безвозвратно потеряна** в subsampled данных (информационный предел — никакая модель её не восстановит). В input остаётся лишь алиас-изображение на f_alias = min_k |f − k/N| < f_Nyq(N). Прогноз: **ни одна модель не должна «восстанавливать» истинную частоту** — метрики фиксируют только правдоподобие генерации; модель может тривиально воспроизвести алиас-изображение, и это должно диагностироваться отдельно.

Разделение на два параллельных arms с разными ожидаемыми исходами делает ответ бинарным и интерпретируемым: Arm A → «может восстановить (band-limited часть)», Arm B → «не может восстановить (потерянную часть), только генерировать правдоподобное».

## 2. Spec синтетического генератора (точно, stdlib: math, random, json)

**Система:** M = 4 torsion angles φ_i(t), i = 1..4, unwrapped radians. **Длина:** T = 4096 full-resolution шагов (t = 0..4095). **Seeds:** S = 20 независимых (random.seed(1000+s)).

**Формула (для каждого угла i):**
φ_i(t) = S_i(t) + A · sin(2π f_i t + φ0_i) + ε_i(t)

- **Медленная компонента** S_i(t): random walk, S_i(0)=0, S_i(t) = S_i(t−1) + N(0, σ_s), σ_s = 0.02 рад/шаг (std на T ≈ 1.3 рад — реалистичный размах; без clamp, зафиксировано как упрощение).
- **Быстрая компонента:** A = 0.3 рад (~17°), φ0_i ~ U[0, 2π) (фикс. seed), чистая синусоида (без затухания — проекции точны; затухающий вариант — опциональная robustness-проверка).
- **Шум** ε_i(t) ~ N(0, σ_e), σ_e = 0.01 рад — присутствует и в full, и в subsampled (subsampled = просто выборка значений).
- **Частоты — целые делители T (нет spectral leakage):** f = k/4096.
  - Arm A: f_A = round(α · T/(2N))/T, α ∈ {0.5, 0.75, 0.9}, с assert f_A < 1/(2N). (N=4: k = 256, 384, 461.)
  - Arm B: f_B = round(β · T/(2N))/T, β ∈ {1.25, 1.5, 1.75}. (N=4: k = 640, 768, 896.) Алиас-изображения: f_alias = {0.75, 0.5, 0.25}·f_Nyq(N) — все строго ниже f_Nyq, т.е. **присутствуют в input** и тривиально восстанавливаемы (это и есть диагностический сигнал Arm B).
  - Каждый угол i получает свою частоту из триплекта (4 угла: 3 частоты + одна повторов для статистики).
- **Subsampled input:** x_k = φ_i(k·N), k = 0..T/N−1. **N ∈ {2, 4, 8}** в обоих arms.
- **Train/test split:** временной — train на первых 75% T, evaluation на последних 25% (temporal generalization).

## 3. Stand-in модель (plan A)

**Авторегрессионный линейный интерполятор** (член класса, без доступа к ground truth при инференсе). Для каждого (arm, N, угол i) отдельная модель. При каждом subsampled k модель генерирует N−1 промежуточных шага:

ŷ_{k,j} = w0 + w1·ŷ_{k,j−1} + w2·x_k + w3·x_{k−1} + w4·(j/N), j = 1..N−1, seed ŷ_{k,0} = x_k.

Обучение: ridge-регрессия (нормальные уравнения 5×5, решаются Гауссом в stdlib) по всем парам (k, j) из train-сплита, target = φ_i(k·N + j). Линейная AR-система с полюсом способен генерировать синусоиду на входной частоте — это честный (хотя и ограниченный по ёмкости) представитель класса. **План B** (если решим, что линейная модель недостаточно representative): та же спецификация с MLP (скрытый слой 16, manual backprop на stdlib) — тот же протокол, больше время; **план B2** (fallback при любом runtime-риске): не-обучаемый parametric fit — по каждому band 2-параметрическая МНК-подгонка a·cos(2πft)+b·sin(2πft) к residual + интерполяционные baselines; проверяет метрики и controls, но не «модель».

## 4. Метрики (точные формулы)

Для ряда y(t), t=0..T−1, на частоте f проекционные коэффициенты:
Ā_f(y) = (2/T)·Σ_t y(t)·cos(2πft); B̄_f(y) = (2/T)·Σ_t y(t)·sin(2πft)
â_f(y) = √(Ā_f² + B̄_f²); θ̂_f(y) = atan2(−B̄_f, Ā_f) (конвенция y ≈ A·cos(2πft+θ)).

Для каждого (seed, N, arm, метод, частота, угол):
1. **R_A(f) = â_f(ŷ)/â_f(y_gt)** — отношение амплитуд (recovery ratio).
2. **Δθ(f) = min_{m∈Z} |θ̂_f(ŷ) − θ_f(gt) − m·2π|** — ошибка фазы (радианы).
3. **SNR_f = â_f(ŷ) / â_f(y_gt − ŷ)** — спектральный SNR восстановления.
4. **Band energy ratio** E_fast(ŷ)/E_fast(y_gt), E_fast = ½·Σ_{f∈F} â_f²; параллельно E_slow (sanity: модель не должна жертвовать медленной компонентой).
5. **RMSE_fast** — RMSE(ŷ − y_gt) после вычитания медленной компоненты (проекция на slow-банд и обратно).
6. **Lag** — сдвиг максимума кросс-корреляции fast-бандов ŷ и y_gt (шаги; ожидается 0).
7. **Диагностическая проекция на f_alias** (только Arm B): â_{f_alias}(ŷ) — показывает, воспроизводит ли модель алиас-изображение вместо истинной частоты.

**Статистика:** по 20 seeds — среднее ± 95% CI; сравнение model vs baseline — paired-тест по seeds (t-тест или знаковый, stdlib). **Пол-шума (noise floor):** проекция y_gt на отсутствующую частоту (напр., 1.5·f) задаёт базовый уровень â, относительно которого судим «≈0».

## 5. Baselines и controls (с ожидаемым поведением каждого)

| # | Control | Arm A (f < f_Nyq) | Arm B (f > f_Nyq) |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **Sinc-интерполяция** Σ_k x_k·sinc((t−kN)/N) — оптимальный band-limited реконструктор | R_A ≈ 1, Δθ мало — **верхняя грань** | R_A(истинная f) ≈ 0; воспроизводит только алиас-банд |
| C2 | **Линейная интерполяция** | R_A < 1, деградирует с ростом N (sinc-откат линейного ядра) | ≈ 0 на истинной f |
| C3 | **Constant hold** (nearest) | R_A ≈ 0 (проходит только slow) | ≈ 0 |
| C4 | **Null-модель** (обучена на target без fast-компоненты) | R_A ≈ 0 — проверяет, что метрики не дают false positive от slow-утечки | ≈ 0 |
| C5 | **Aliasing-диагностика** (проекции на f_alias + аудит input): â_f(x_subsampled) на истинной f_B ≈ 0 (input не содержит истинную частоту); â_{f_alias}(ŷ) велик | — | Если R_A(истинная f) вдруг высока → искать утечку/запоминание, а не «восстановление» |
| C6 | **N-sweep** N ∈ {2,4,8} | Кривая recovery vs N (деградация при приближении f к f_Nyq) | Плоское ≈ 0 на истинной f |
| C7 | **Leave-one-frequency-out** (train на 2 из 3 частот, test на 3-й) | Performance сохраняется → обобщение, не запоминание | ≈ 0 |
| C8 | **Metric null** (проекция GT на отсутствующую частоту) | задаёт noise floor для всех «≈0» | то же |
| C9 (опц.) | **Cross-arm** (train на A, test на B) | — | Ожидается провал — подтверждение режима |

## 6. Analysis plan и pass/fail критерии

1. Генерация датасетов (seeds × N × arms → JSON/CSV в workspace).
2. Обучение stand-in per (arm, N, угол) на train-сплите; прогон всех baselines (без обучения).
3. Расчёт метрик §4 per (seed, N, arm, метод, частота, угол) → агрегация.
4. **Критерий Arm A («восстанавливает band-limited fast dynamics»):** R_A(model) ≥ 0.8 · R_A(sinc) И R_A(model) ≥ 1.2 · R_A(линейная) И Δθ ≤ 0.25 рад И R_A(null) < 0.2 · R_A(sinc).
5. **Критерий Arm B («не восстанавливает потерянную»):** R_A(истинная f) ≤ noise floor + 2σ (т.е. ≲ 0.15) для ВСЕХ методов, включая model; C5 фиксирует, что энергия модели в Arm B сидит на f_alias, а не на истинной f.
6. **Итоговый ответ на вопрос (шаблон):** «Модели класса MDGEN способны точно восстанавливать band-limited часть быстрых dynamics (результат Arm A: цифры), но не способны восстанавливать aliased/безвозвратно потерянную часть (Arm B: цифры); для последней они могут лишь генерировать правдоподобные осцилляции, что метрики recovery не могут отличить от восстановления без ground truth».
7. Отчёт: markdown с таблицами (метод × N × arm × метрика), expected-vs-observed по каждому control, caveat §0, limitations.

## 7. Feasibility

- **stdlib-only** (math, random, json, csv, statistics) — подтверждено: numpy/scipy отсутствуют, сеть выключена.
- **Runtime (оценка, не замер):** генерация 20×3×2×4×4096 значений — секунды; 24 ridge-регрессии (5 признаков, ~10^5 образцов, системы 5×5) — секунды; проекции ~3.2×10^8 умножений в чистом Python — ~минута. **Итого ≪ 30 мин CPU**, GPU не нужен. Риск runtime низкий; план B/B2 — страховка.
- Детерминизм: все seeds фиксированы → воспроизводимость.

## 8. Limitations (обязательно в отчёте)

1. **Stand-in ≠ реальный MDGEN** — ответ на уровне класса моделей; для конкретного MDGEN дизайн переносим 1:1 (заменить заглушку на реальную модель, остальная инфраструктура метрик/controls не меняется).
2. Синтетические torsion dynamics (независимые синусоиды + random walk) не включают связанную многотельную динамику, сохранение энергии, нелинейности/ангармоничность; «fast dynamics» проксируются синусоидами.
3. Unwrapped углы, независимые torsion angles, одна «система» — нет обобщения по молекулам.

## 1. Inspección del input / repo

**Resultado: el workspace está esencialmente vacío.** `/workspace` contiene un único archivo, `task.json`, con: la pregunta, el contexto ("Design an experiment that answers the question... Do not claim that an experiment was run"), y un documento `track.md` de una sola línea: *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."*

Explícitamente **NO hay**:
- ❌ Código de MDGEN ni de ningún generador de MD
- ❌ Trajectories (subsampled o full-rate), datasets ni configs
- ❌ Paper, README ni documentación de referencia
- ❌ Entorno con dependencias (Python 3.14.4 system, sin GPU, red deshabilitada — verificado)

**Consecuencia para el diseño:** todo el experimento debe ser auto-contenido y referenciar la literatura MDGEN como fuente de especificación del modelo (el MDGEN canónico es el modelo de difusión sobre dinámicas moleculares de Ogbele et al., *Nature Methods* 2024). No puedo verificar ese paper desde el sandbox (red off), así que sus detalles exactos van en "supuestos".

---

## 2. Enfoque propuesto (esqueleto, no desarrollo completo)

### (a) Métricas de "fast dynamics" (todas sobre dihedrals, por residuo y agregadas)
1. **PSD (power spectral density)** de φ(t) por dihedral + promedio de ensemble, con énfasis en la **banda alta** (por encima de la frecuencia de Nyquist del input subsampleado — ahí el input no tiene información, así que cualquier señal es "reconstruida" por el modelo).
2. **Autocorrelation time τ** (integral de ACF) de φ(t) y de Δφ(t).
3. **RMSF / varianza** de los dihedrals.
4. **RMSD del incremento por paso** (Δφ entre frames consecutivos) — sensible a la dinámica rápida sin importar la deriva lenta.
5. **Frecuencia de cruce de barrera** entre estados del dihedral (p. ej., rotamers) — captura la dinámica rápida *consecuencial*, no solo ruido.

Cada métrica se reporta en dos bandas: *recuperable* (debajo del Nyquist del input) y *no recuperable* (por encima). Esta separación es el corazón del diseño: distingue lo que el modelo podría inferir del input de lo que solo podría hallucinar desde su prior.

### (b) Ground truth de la dinámica rápida
- **MD full-timestep** (p. ej., 1–2 fs) del sistema, mismo force field, mismas condiciones iniciales que la fuente del input → es la referencia de "la" dinámica.
- **Input subsampleado** = decimación uniforme del full-rate por factor k (mantener cada k-ésimo frame).
- **Pipeline de evaluación:** MDGEN se entrena sobre trayectorias subsampleadas (o full, según el diseño original) y se le pide **generar/interpolar los frames faltantes** condicionando en el input; se compara su output full-rate contra el ground truth full-rate.
- **Punto clave de diseño (identificabilidad):** con subsampling uniforme, los frames intermedios verdaderos **no son identificables** a partir del input solo (infinitas trayectorias continuas son consistentes). Por tanto, "recuperar" debe definirse como: *la generación es una muestra plausible de la distribución condicional de la dinámica verdadera dado el input* — y medimos qué tan cerca está de la realización verdadera.

### (c) Controles y ablations
- **C1 — Upper bound:** MDGEN recibe la trayectoria full (k=1) → ¿recupera ~identidad?
- **C2 — Baseline sin modelo:** interpolación lineal / hold-last-frame del subsampleado → piso de las métricas.
- **C3 — Floor estocástico:** input de frames *shuffled/independientes* → si MDGEN igual produce "buenas" PSDs, está generando desde su prior, no recuperando del input.
- **C4 — Out-of-distribution:** MDGEN entrenado en otro sistema / otro k → separa memorización de generalización.
- **Ablations:** factor k (4, 8, 16, 32); tipo de dihedral (backbone ψ/ω vs. side-chain χ1–χ3); tamaño del sistema; nº de replicados MD independientes y seeds de generación.

### (d) Recuperación vs. simulación estocástica
Criterio central: **comparar métricas per-sample vs. métricas de ensemble.**
- Si la generación correlaciona frame-a-frame con los frames intermedios *verdaderos* (correlación de Δφ alta, ~1) → **recuperación** genuina (el modelo invierte el subsampling).
- Si solo las estadísticas de ensemble (PSD promedio, RMSF) cuadran pero la correlación per-sample es baja → **simulación estocástica**: muestrea de la distribución de dinámicas, no recupera *la* dinámica.
- Test de diagnóstico adicional: **likelihood condicional** — ¿las frames verdaderas caen en región de alta probabilidad del modelo (score/energy del denoised)? → separa "muestra plausible" de "reconstrucción".
- Firma esperada de recuperación real: el error per-sample **decrece cuando k baja**; una simulación estocástica no mostraría esa tendencia.

---

## 3. Supuestos e incertidumbres (marcado por impacto)

| # | Supuesto | Impacto si cambia |
|---|----------|-------------------|
| **A1** | "MDGEN" = modelo de difusión de Ogbele et al. 2024 (Nature Methods), condicionado en frames observados | 🔴 **Alto** — si es otro generador (p. ej., LSTM-based, o condicionado en geometría completa en vez de torsions), el test recuperación-vs-simulación (d) y el pipeline (b) cambian sustancialmente |
| **A2** | Sistema: pequeña proteína o péptido en agua (~100–500 residuos), force field estándar (AMBER ff14sb), NVT/NPT, T=300K | 🟡 Medio — el diseño es invariante al sistema, pero cambia presupuesto de cómputo y selección de dihedrals |
| **A3** | Timestep original 1–2 fs; k ∈ {4, 8, 16, 32} (input efectivo 4–64 fs) | 🔴 **Alto** — k define la banda de Nyquist y, por tanto, qué fracción de la dinámica rápida es en principio recuperable; k grande → la pregunta se vuelve "¿hallucina dinámicas plausibles?" en vez de "¿recupera?" |
| **A4** | Se puede correr MD full-timestep (ground truth) con las mismas CIs | 🔴 **Alto** — si no hay compute, el diseño degrada a validar solo estadísticas de ensemble contra el input (perdemos el test per-sample de (d), que es la parte más fuerte) |
| **A5** | MDGEN se condiciona solo en frames observados subsampleados (sin restraints de distancia/backbone) | 🟡 Medio — si hay condiciones extra, el espacio de "trayectorias consistentes" se acota y la recuperabilidad mejora |
| **A6** | "Fast" = banda por encima del Nyquist del input; dihedrals con τc ~ 0.1–10 ps | 🟡 Medio — si el interés está en vibraciones atómicas (fs), ni el subsampleado ni el modelo de torsions las capturan; hay que acotar la pregunta a la escala ps |
| **A7** | GPU disponible en la fase de ejecución (hoy: no hay GPU, solo diseño) | 🟢 Bajo para el diseño, alto para factibilidad — el diseño debe especificar presupuesto (repl × longitud × seeds) para que sea ejecutable |

**Los tres que más cambian el diseño: A1, A3 y A4.** A1 porque define qué modelo estamos probando; A3 porque define qué es recuperable en principio; A4 porque define si podemos hacer el test per-sample (el más discriminatorio) o solo el de ensemble.

---

**Peticiones de aclaración sugeridas (si el researcher quiere afinar, tema por tema):** (1) ¿qué implementación/paper de MDGEN exactamente? (2) ¿sistema y k objetivo? (3) ¿hay presupuesto de MD full-rate disponible?
