payload.answer:
# Experiment Design: The Effect of QuaRot's Hadamard Transformation on Weight-Only Quantization Quality at 2–4 Bits

## 1. Objective and research questions

This document specifies a complete, self-contained experiment to answer two questions about weight-only low-precision quantization of large language models. The experiment has not been run; it is a design-only deliverable, and no result reported in this document is a measured outcome.

Part (a) asks *how* the Hadamard transformation used in QuaRot improves the quality of weight-only quantized models under low-precision settings. The working hypothesis, drawn from the QuaRot paper, is that outlier dimensions in LLM weights (a small number of entries whose magnitude is orders of magnitude above the mean) force per-group quantizers to waste most of the representable range on a handful of values, corrupting the long tail of small weights. Applying a random orthogonal Hadamard rotation W → WH before quantization spreads that outlier energy uniformly across dimensions, making the per-group weight distribution approximately Gaussian and therefore well matched to a symmetric affine codebook. Part (a) is therefore not merely "does QuaRot help" but "does the rotation reduce outlier-driven quantization error, and does that reduction propagate to downstream quality."

Part (b) asks whether QuaRot *stabilizes and improves* performance at 2–4 bit weight precision, i.e., in the regime where RTN and GPTQ degrade sharply or collapse. "Stabilize" is interpreted operationally (Section 5b): a method is judged to fail at a given (model, bit-width, metric) cell if degradation crosses a pre-registered threshold, and QuaRot is said to stabilize performance if its failure rate across cells is substantially lower than RTN's and GPTQ's at 2 and 3 bits, while its quality is at least as good as the best baseline at 4 bits.

Two design principles follow. First, the method effect must be separated from the algorithm effect: QuaRot (rotation + RTN) versus RTN confounds the rotation with the choice of error-minimizing vs. round-to-nearest algorithm, so the experiment includes a fourth arm, Hadamard-GPTQ, which differs from GPTQ by exactly the rotation. Second, the mechanism claim of part (a) requires weight-level diagnostics (outlier statistics, per-layer quantization error) in addition to task-level metrics, so that a causal chain — rotation reduces outliers → outliers reduce per-layer quantization error → error reduction reduces perplexity/task degradation — can be checked link by link.

## 2. Experimental design

### 2.1 Independent variables

The experiment is a factorial over two independent variables. The first is bit-width W ∈ {4, 3, 2}, applied identically to every arm. The second is the quantization method, with four arms described below. A third, within-arm variable is the Hadamard seed (Section 2.5), which varies only for the two rotation arms. Model is a blocking variable (Section 2.3), not a free factor: all arms and bit-widths are run on the same models so that every comparison is within-model.

### 2.2 The four arms and exact quantization configuration

All arms share one quantization configuration unless stated otherwise: per-group symmetric affine quantization with group size g = 128; the scale of each group is (max |w| − min |w|)/(2^W − 1) computed on the (possibly rotated) weights, offsets are not used (symmetric), and quantized codes are stored as W-bit integers. All linear layers of the model — attention projections (q, k, v, o), feed-forward up/down projections, and the language-model head (lm_head) — are quantized. Input token embeddings are kept in FP16. This layer selection matches the QuaRot paper's weight-only setting and the standard GPTQ configuration; it is flagged as assumption A10.

Arm 1, RTN: round-to-nearest quantization of the original weights with the shared configuration. No calibration data is used; the method is fully deterministic. This is the no-calibration baseline.

Arm 2, GPTQ: the Hessian-approximation, error-minimizing quantization of Frantar & Alistarh. Each linear layer is quantized by greedily choosing codes that minimize ‖WX − Q̂X‖² subject to a sparsity-ordered update, using the exact per-layer Hessian X X^T accumulated over the calibration set, with the standard Cholesky-factored inverse-Hessian schedule and oblique projection. GPTQ uses the same group size, symmetric per-group scaling, and layer set as RTN, so the only differences from Arm 1 are the use of the Hessian and the calibration data. GPTQ is deterministic given fixed calibration data and seed.

Arm 3, QuaRot (weight-only variant): each linear weight W is replaced by W' = W H, where H = (1/√d) S₁ H_d S₂ is a random orthogonal Hadamard matrix — S₁ and S₂ are independent random diagonal matrices with ±1 entries drawn from a fixed seed, and H_d is the size-d Walsh–Hadamard matrix (composed of tensor products of 2×2 Hadamard blocks, so it is applied in O(d log d) time). W' is quantized with the same per-group symmetric affine RTN configuration as Arm 1. At inference, the dequantized Ŵ' is multiplied by H on the activation side: Ŷ = X H Ŵ'^T, exploiting H = H^T and H^T H = I. The Hadamard application to activations is a runtime arithmetic operation, not activation quantization, so this arm respects the weight-only constraint. Note that the full QuaRot system also includes SmoothQuant activation smoothing; that component is an activation-side technique and is explicitly out of scope here, so this arm is the paper's weight-only component (Hadamard + RTN). This scoping is flagged as assumption A12 and as limitation L1.

Arm 4, Hadamard-GPTQ: the same rotation W' = W H is applied first, and GPTQ is then run on the rotated model — critically, the per-layer Hessian is recomputed on the rotated network (a forward pass of the rotated model over the calibration set), so the Hessian reflects the rotated weight/activation geometry rather than being carried over from the unrotated model. This arm differs from Arm 2 by exactly the rotation, and is the clean ablation that isolates the Hadamard step at fixed algorithm. It is the central comparison for part (a).

### 2.3 Model selection and justification

Three models are used: LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and Mistral-7B-v0.1. The justification is threefold. First, the QuaRot paper reports results on LLaMA-2, LLaMA-3, and Mistral, so using the same families makes the design's claims source-consistent and permits direct comparison with published numbers. Second, 7–13B models are the scale at which weight-outlier structure is pronounced and 2-bit quantization is visibly destructive; smaller models show the phenomenon less sharply. Third, including two different architectures (LLaMA and Mistral, with different attention variants and vocabularies) tests whether the conclusion is family-specific, which is necessary before claiming that QuaRot "stabilizes" 2–4 bit quantization generally rather than for one family. A 3B model would have been the minimal-budget alternative and a 70B model the maximal-strength alternative; both are rejected on budget grounds (Section 6) and noted as assumption A2.

### 2.4 Calibration data (GPTQ arms only)

RTN and QuaRot require no calibration. GPTQ and Hadamard-GPTQ use a fixed calibration set: 256 sequences of 2048 tokens sampled from the C4 validation split (en-10.0.0), using the standard GPTQ sampling procedure with a fixed sampling seed (42) and standard tokenization per model. The same calibration set is used for every model, every bit-width, and every seed of the two GPTQ arms, so calibration is a controlled variable, not a free one. Hadamard-GPTQ uses the identical sampling seed and sequences; only the forward pass (hence the Hessian) differs because the weights are rotated.

### 2.5 Seed strategy

The two rotation arms depend on the random sign matrices S₁, S₂. For each (model, W) cell, K = 5 independent Hadamard seeds are drawn from a documented list (e.g., 0–4), and each seed produces a fully independent quantized model and evaluation. This matters most at 2 bits, where rotation variance is largest and "stabilization" claims would otherwise amount to a single lucky draw; K = 5 supports variance estimates and paired tests. RTN and GPTQ are deterministic under fixed configuration and calibration, so they require a single run per cell. Total quantization runs: RTN 3 models × 3 W = 9; GPTQ 9; QuaRot 45; Hadamard-GPTQ 45; plus 3 FP16 reference evaluations.

## 3. Controls

Every variable that is not the target of a comparison is held constant across arms, and each control is listed with the reason it must be controlled. Group size g = 128 is identical across all four arms, because group size independently changes quantization granularity and would otherwise confound the method effect; a g ∈ {64, 256} sensitivity sweep is listed as assumption A7 but is not in the main design. Symmetric per-group affine scaling is used by all arms, because mixing symmetric and asymmetric codebooks would introduce a second algorithmic difference. The layer set (all linears including lm_head, embeddings FP16) is identical, because different layer coverage changes total effective bit-count and quality. The FP16/BF16 reference is the original, unmodified checkpoint for each model, evaluated with identical batching, sequence length, and prompt templates as the quantized models, so that every degradation number is a within-model difference. The calibration set is fixed in content, size, order, and sampling seed for both GPTQ arms, because GPTQ quality is sensitive to calibration data and an uncontrolled difference would corrupt the GPTQ-vs-Hadamard-GPTQ contrast. Evaluation protocol — dataset splits, prompt templates, batch size, seed for any stochastic decoding (all tasks here are greedy, so none), and hardware — is identical across arms, because benchmark harness differences are a known source of spurious perplexity deltas of the same order as the effects being measured. Hardware is a single node with the same GPU for all runs, because quantization kernels and precision of the dequantized matmul (FP16 accumulate of dequantized-to-FP16 weights) must be the same everywhere. Finally, the bit-width is applied identically to every arm, and dequantization at inference uses the same FP16 dequantized matmul in all arms, so the measured differences come from the quantization method alone, not from inference precision.

## 4. Evaluation protocol

### 4.1 Language-modeling perplexity

Zero-shot perplexity is computed on three held-out sets: WikiText-2 (test), C4 (validation, 256K-token window), and PTB (test), using the standard next-token evaluation with sequence length 2048 and batch 8, identical for FP16 and all quantized models. Perplexity is reported both as the absolute value and as relative degradation ΔPPL = (PPL_quant − PPL_FP16)/PPL_FP16. Three sets are used because the three corpora have different vocabulary coverage and domain, and a method that fails on one but not another is not "stabilized."

### 4.2 Zero-shot task suite

Six zero-shot tasks are evaluated with the lm-evaluation-harness, greedy decoding, default templates: LAMBADA (last-word prediction), PIQA (physical commonsense), ARC-e (science reasoning), WinoGrande (coreference), TruthfulQA (multiple-choice), and RTE (entailment). Accuracy is reported per task as FP16 value and Δaccuracy. The suite mixes generation-style and multiple-choice formats and spans commonsense, reasoning, and truthfulness, so that "quality" is not a single-number construct.

### 4.3 FP16 reference

For each model, the unmodified checkpoint is evaluated once on all three perplexity sets and all six tasks, with the exact protocol of 4.1 and 4.2. These nine numbers per model are the denominator of every degradation metric and the anchor of the failure rule; they are computed once and reused, never re-sampled.

### 4.4 Mechanism diagnostics (for part (a))

Three weight-level measurements are taken per layer, per model, and per arm: (i) outlier statistics — the ratio of maximum to mean absolute weight magnitude, the kurtosis of the weight distribution, and the effective number of bits (the entropy of the quantization codebook usage, i.e., how many of the 2^W codes are actually used, or equivalently 1 − normalized quantization MSE) — computed both on the original weights and, for the rotation arms, on the rotated weights W H; (ii) per-layer relative quantization error ‖Q(W) − W‖_F / ‖W‖_F (and, for rotation arms, ‖Q(WH)H^T − W‖_F / ‖W‖_F, which is the error the model actually sees); (iii) the Spearman correlation, across layers, between each layer's pre-rotation outlier ratio and its pre-rotation quantization error, and the same correlation computed post-rotation for the rotation arms. The predicted signature of the mechanism is: pre-rotation, high outlier ratio correlates strongly with high quantization error; post-rotation, outlier ratios are compressed across layers, the correlation weakens, and per-layer error drops in absolute terms. If QuaRot beats RTN but this signature is absent, the gain has a different cause and part (a) must be answered accordingly — the diagnostics are what make the "how" question answerable rather than merely correlational.

## 5. Analysis plan

### 5(a) Attributing quality gains to the Hadamard rotation

The rotation effect is estimated from two contrasts at each (model, W): C1 = RTN − QuaRot, which isolates rotation under RTN, and C2 = GPTQ − Hadamard-GPTQ, which isolates rotation under GPTQ. The causal chain is checked in three steps. Step 1 (rotation → outliers): compare pre/post-rotation outlier statistics; the expected result is a large drop in max/mean ratio and kurtosis in the rotated weights. Step 2 (outliers → error): compare the layer-level error-vs-outlier correlation pre- vs. post-rotation and the absolute per-layer relative quantization error of QuaRot vs. RTN and Hadamard-GPTQ vs. GPTQ; the expected result is a weaker correlation and lower error after rotation. Step 3 (error → quality): compare ΔPPL and Δaccuracy of the paired contrasts C1 and C2; the expected result is that the arms with lower weight-level error have lower quality degradation. If C1 and C2 both favor the rotated arm and steps 1–2 show the diagnostic signature, the gain is attributed to the rotation specifically; if only C1 (or only C2) favors rotation, the effect is algorithm-conditional; if the diagnostics show no outlier compression, the claim of part (a) is not supported and the design has failed in the informative direction.

### 5(b) Operational failure definition and sensitivity analysis

A method is declared to **fail** at a (model, W, metric) cell if any of the following holds: ΔPPL > 100% over the FP16 reference, or absolute PPL > 10, or Δaccuracy > 20 percentage points on any of the six tasks. The three clauses are pre-registered together with their rationale: the relative PPL clause captures multiplicative collapse (the typical 2-bit GPTQ/RTN failure mode), the absolute PPL clause captures cases where the FP16 baseline is already weak, and the accuracy clause captures task-level collapse that perplexity may miss. Part (b) is then answered by tabulating, for each method and each W ∈ {4, 3, 2}, the fraction of cells across the 3 models × 9 metrics in which the method fails, plus the worst-cell degradation. QuaRot "stabilizes" 2–3 bit quantization if its failure fraction at W = 2 and W = 3 is materially lower than both RTN's and GPTQ's, and "improves" if its mean degradation at those widths is lower than both baselines'. A sensitivity analysis repeats the failure tabulation at 50% and 150% of each threshold (i.e., ΔPPL > 50%/150%, PPL > 5/15, Δacc > 10/30 pts) to show that the conclusion is not an artifact of the exact cutoff. The pre-registration of the thresholds and the sensitivity sweep are the guard against post-hoc threshold shopping.

### 5(c) Statistical tests, effect sizes, and confidence intervals

All method comparisons are paired within (model, W, seed) cells: the two arms in a contrast are evaluated on identical data with identical protocol, so per-cell paired differences are the unit of analysis. For each contrast and metric, the paired difference (e.g., ΔPPL_GPTQ − ΔPPL_HadGPTQ at W, model, seed) is tested with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (non-parametric because 2-bit degradation distributions are heavy-tailed and n per contrast is small: 5 seeds × 3 models = 15 pairs for rotation arms, 3 pairs for the deterministic-arm contrasts — the latter are reported descriptively with CIs rather than tested), with the rank-biserial correlation r as the effect size. 95% confidence intervals are computed by non-parametric bootstrap (10,000 resamples over the seed × model pairs) on the mean paired difference. Because the full analysis involves many cells (4 methods × 3 W × 3 models × 9 metrics), no multiplicity correction is applied to the primary table, but a Bonferroni-corrected version of the W = 2 and W = 3 comparisons is reported as a robustness check, and all cells — including null ones — are reported in the main table.

## 6. Feasibility

This is a **design-only deliverable; no experiment has been run**, and nothing in this document is a measured result. Feasibility is stated for a standard execution environment (not the current sandbox, which is CPU-only, network-disabled, and contains no code or data). Hardware budget: 1–2× NVIDIA A100-80GB (or equivalent) per model, single node; 80GB is required to hold a 13B model in FP16 plus GPTQ's Hessian workspace. Estimated wall time per run: RTN quantization of a 7–13B model at g = 128 takes on the order of 10–30 minutes; QuaRot adds the O(d log d) rotation, negligible; GPTQ takes on the order of 1–3 hours per (model, W) including the Hessian forward pass, and Hadamard-GPTQ is comparable plus the rotation. Evaluation of one quantized model on the three PPL sets plus six tasks takes on the order of 1–2 hours on a single A100. Per (model, W) cell the cost is therefore roughly: RTN ≈ 1.5–2 h, GPTQ ≈ 3–5 h, QuaRot ≈ 1.5–2 h (×5 seeds), Hadamard-GPTQ ≈ 3–5 h (×5 seeds), giving ≈ 30–40 GPU-hours per (model, W) cell, ≈ 90–120 per model, and ≈ 270–360 GPU-hours total for 3 models × 3 W × 4 arms (with seed multiplicity) plus 3 FP16 references. On 1× A100 this is roughly 12–15 days; on 2× A100 (models parallelized) roughly 6–8 days; a realistic single-team budget is **1–2× A100-80GB for 3–7 calendar days**, dominated by the 90 seeded rotation-arm runs. A reduced-budget variant (drop Mistral, K = 3 seeds) cuts this by roughly half. Software: the official QuaRot repository (Hadamard construction, rotation, and weight-only quantization), GPTQModel (or the original GPTQ-for-LLaMa code) for the GPTQ arms, Hugging Face Transformers for model loading and the FP16 reference, and lm-evaluation-harness for the task suite. One-time network access is needed at setup to fetch model weights and code; no network is needed during the runs. Storage: ≈ 3 models × ~25 GB FP16 ≈ 75 GB, plus quantized checkpoints (2–4 bits) totaling under 50 GB.

## 7. Assumptions and limitations

The following assumptions were flagged at the planning stage and are carried forward with their alternatives; they are choices, not fixed constraints. A1: Model family LLaMA-2 7B/13B + Mistral-7B — matters because the outlier phenomenon and the paper's comparability both depend on family; alternative: GPT-2 (weak outliers) or a single 3B model (cheapest). A2: Size band 7–13B — 2-bit effects are most visible at ≥7B; alternatives: 3B-only (minimal budget) or 70B (strongest claim, ~10× budget). A3: Calibration data C4 validation, 256 × 2048 tokens, seed 42 — affects only the two GPTQ arms but must be identical across them; alternative: WikiText-2 train split. A4: Benchmarks = 3 PPL sets + 6 zero-shot tasks — alternatives: PPL-only (cheaper, under-characterizes quality) or the full ~10-task suite (more expensive). A5: Failure rule ΔPPL > 100% / PPL > 10 / Δacc > 20 pts, pre-registered with sensitivity at 50%/150% — the entire part-(b) conclusion hinges on it; alternative: relative-only threshold or qualitative judgment. A6: Hadamard-GPTQ included as the fourth arm — without it, rotation and algorithm effects are confounded; alternative: drop it (weaker causal attribution). A7: Group size g = 128, symmetric per-group affine — matches standard QuaRot/GPTQ configuration; alternative: g ∈ {64, 256} sensitivity sweep (≈2× runs). A8: K = 5 Hadamard seeds per rotation-arm cell — needed to support "stabilize" claims at 2-bit; alternative: K = 1 (cheapest, but cannot distinguish stabilization from luck). A9: Wilcoxon signed-rank + rank-biserial r + bootstrap CIs, no primary multiplicity correction, Bonferroni as robustness check — alternative: plain mean±std reporting. A10: All linear layers including lm_head quantized, input embeddings FP16 — paper-consistent; alternative: keep lm_head FP16 (would flatter all arms equally). A11: Feasibility budget 1–2× A100-80GB, 3–7 days — the feasibility claim must name a concrete budget; alternative: single 40GB card, 7B-only. A12: Scope excludes SmoothQuant activation smoothing, activation quantization, and residual quantization — these are activation-side or out-of-scope components; alternative: include a runtime-overhead micro-benchmark as a secondary metric.

New limitations arising in the full write-up. L1: The "QuaRot" arm is the paper's weight-only component (Hadamard + per-group RTN), not the full QuaRot system with SmoothQuant; results therefore answer the question as scoped (weight-only), but any comparison with the paper's full-system numbers must keep this scoping in mind. L2: The Hadamard-GPTQ arm requires recomputing the Hessian on the rotated model; if an implementation carries the unrotated Hessian over, the arm is not the intended ablation — this must be verified in the implementation before runs. L3: The deterministic arms (RTN, GPTQ) have only 3 pairs per contrast (one per model), so their contrasts are reported descriptively with CIs rather than hypothesis-tested; the statistical power for part (a) rests on the 15-pair rotation contrasts. L4: The failure rule's accuracy clause (Δacc > 20 pts) is coarse for tasks whose FP16 accuracy is already high (e.g., PIQA), where a 20-point drop is near-impossible; the PPL clauses carry most of the part-(b) signal, and this asymmetry should be noted when interpreting the failure table. L5: Perplexity and task degradation are evaluated on a single prompt set per task (harness defaults); harness template or prompt-sampling differences across versions could shift absolute numbers, so the harness version must be pinned. L6: All conclusions are specific to the three models and three widths tested; generalization to other architectures, sizes, or W = 1 requires further runs. L7: The design assumes the named open-source implementations correctly implement the described configurations; a pre-flight sanity check (reproduce a published RTN/GPTQ 4-bit perplexity number within tolerance on LLaMA-2-7B) is recommended before the full grid is launched.

A reader with access to the named implementations (QuaRot repository, GPTQModel, Transformers, lm-evaluation-harness), the three model checkpoints, and 1–2× A100-80GB can execute this experiment from this document alone: quantize each model under each arm and bit-width with the seeds and calibration set specified, evaluate on the specified protocol, compute the specified diagnostics, and apply the specified analysis. No experiment has been run in producing this document.

WORKSPACE INSPECTION (findings)
- /workspace contains ONLY task.json. No code, no QuaRot implementation, no configs, no datasets, no prior scaffolding. Effectively empty.
- task.json = the question + a note "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."
- Environment: Python 3.14.4, system Python; NO ML stack preinstalled (no torch/transformers/gptq/auto-gptq/lm-eval). Network is DISABLED (HuggingFace unreachable). gpu_enabled=false, 224 CPU cores.
- Implication: this is a pure design deliverable. The design must specify exact pinned library versions, checkpoint ids, dataset ids, and calibration sets so it is reproducible elsewhere, since nothing is pre-provisioned here.

PROPOSED APPROACH (skeleton)

1) Baselines in scope — all FOUR:
   - RTN (round-to-nearest, symmetric, per-group) — non-QuaRot
   - GPTQ — non-QuaRot
   - QuaRot-RTN (rotation + RTN)
   - QuaRot-GPTQ (rotation + GPTQ)
   The question explicitly contrasts RTN vs GPTQ under QuaRot, and "how well does QuaRot generalize" requires the non-QuaRot RTN/GPTQ as the reference pair. So: 4 quantization configs x 3 bit-widths (INT4/6/8) = 12 quantized points, plus 1 FP16/BF16 unquantized reference = 13 cells.

2) Perplexity:
   - Corpus: WikiText-103 test split (standard for LLM quant papers; ~4.7M tokens). Fallback: C4 validation if licensing/availability is a concern.
   - Tokens: full test set (~4.7M) for the headline number; report on 512-token windows, sliding, standard eval loop.
   - Context length: model supports 4K, but QuaRot paper uses 2048; I propose 2048 for parity with the source, and note 4096 as a sensitivity check. Flag: choosing 2048 vs 4096 is a consequential, source-parity decision.

3) Zero-shot accuracy:
   - Use lm-evaluation-harness. Primary suite: HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, WinoGrande (the standard 5-task zero-shot set used in quantization papers). Justification: broad coverage, zero-shot, cheap, directly comparable to QuaRot's reported metrics. Optionally add OBQA (hard, small n=500) only if compute permits; I lean to keeping the core 5.

4) INT6 handling (NON-STANDARD — flagged as assumption):
   - QuaRot does not clearly specify 6-bit group sizes/codebook width. Proposal: treat 6-bit as a symmetric 6-bit integer codebook (levels = 2^6 = 64) with the SAME group size used for 4-bit (g=128) to keep the only moving variable = bit-width. For QuaRot, the Hadamard/rotation is applied identically; only the codebook width changes. I will explicitly flag that 6-bit is a design assumption not pinned by the paper, and that GPTQ's Hessian-based quantization at 6 levels is supported by the GPTQ formulation (arbitrary integer levels).

5) GPTQ calibration:
   - Calibration set: C4 (the default/standard GPTQ calibration corpus), 128 sequences, 2048 tokens each (matches QuaRot/GPTQ convention). Alternative: ~128 samples from a neutral mix. Flag as a parameter to pin.

CONTROLS
- Unquantized reference: FP16 (and BF16 if the checkpoint is BF16-native) Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, same eval pipeline. This is the "no quantization" anchor.
- Standard (non-QuaRot) RTN and GPTQ at the same INT4/6/8 widths serve as the baselines that isolate QuaRot's contribution (i.e., the delta QuaRot-RTN vs RTN and QuaRot-GPTQ vs GPTQ is the generalization signal).

CONSEQUENTIAL ASSUMPTIONS & UNCERTAINTIES (to flag in final design)
A1. Checkpoint: assume the INSTRUCT-tuned "microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct" (per the question), NOT the base "Phi-3-mini-4k". Consequential because perplexity/accuracy differ; the question names instruct explicitly.
A2. QuaRot architecture applicability: Phi-3 uses GQA (grouped-query attention) and SwiGLU FFN. QuaRot's rotations are designed for standard LLaMA-style attention/MLP; whether the Hadamard/rotation retraining applies to Phi-3's GQA head layout and SwiGLU gates WITHOUT modification is an OPEN RISK. I will note it as a feasibility caveat rather than assume it works.
A3. Library versions: MUST pin a specific QuaRot release (the NeuronAI/QuaRot repo, a dated commit) and a specific GPTQ implementation. I propose QuaRot from the official repo + GPTQModel (gptqmodel) for the non-QuaRot GPTQ baseline, and QuaRot's own GPTQ path for QuaRot-GPTQ. Flag: AutoGPTQ vs GPTQModel choice is consequential for reproducibility. lm-eval-harness version must also be pinned.
A4. 6-bit is an assumption (see #4) — not paper-pinned.
A5. Compute/GPU: design assumes a single modern GPU (e.g., A100/H100) with enough VRAM for the ~3.8B model at these widths; this environment has no GPU, so feasibility is assessed on target-hardware assumptions, not this sandbox.

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design: QuaRot Generalization to Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (INT4/6/8)

**Goal.** Measure how well QuaRot's rotation-based quantization transfers to a non-LLaMA model (Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, GQA + SwiGLU) by comparing RTN vs GPTQ under QuaRot against their non-QuaRot counterparts, in perplexity and zero-shot accuracy at 4/6/8 bits. The **primary signal is the QuaRot delta**, not absolute numbers. Design-only: no experiment was run here.

---

## 1. Rationale
- QuaRot is validated on LLaMA-family models; Phi-3 differs architecturally (Grouped-Query Attention, SwiGLU FFN, no tie-embed, rotary + logit-softcap). Testing it isolates whether the rotation mechanism is architecture-agnostic.
- Contrasting RTN vs GPTQ *within* QuaRot and *outside* QuaRot lets us decompose: (i) QuaRot's gain over plain RTN/GPTQ (generalization) and (ii) whether QuaRot's benefit is larger for RTN than GPTQ (as in the paper, where QuaRot-RTN recovers most of QuaRot-GPTQ's quality at lower cost).
- Three bit-widths (4/6/8) expose where rotation helps most (low-bit) and whether 6-bit behaves as expected.

## 2. Fixed requirements (from the question, not assumptions)
- Model: **`microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct`** (instruct-tuned, ~3.8B). Base model is OUT of scope.
- Bit-widths: **INT4, INT6, INT8** (symmetric).
- Metrics: **perplexity** and **zero-shot accuracy**.

## 3. Method matrix (13 cells)
| # | Config | Quantizer | 4-bit | 6-bit | 8-bit |
|---|--------|-----------|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 0 | FP ref | none (BF16/FP16) | — | — | — |
| 1 | RTN | GPTQModel RTN | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| 2 | GPTQ | GPTQModel GPTQ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| 3 | QuaRot-RTN | QuaRot (rotation + RTN) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| 4 | QuaRot-GPTQ | QuaRot (rotation + GPTQ) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

- **Group size g = 128** for all (QuaRot/GPTQ default); no act/weight mixed precision beyond the integer width.
- **6-bit = 64-level symmetric codebook**, reusing g=128. *Design assumption: the QuaRot paper does not pin 6-bit group size/codebook; we hold group size constant so bit-width is the only moving variable.*
- Quantize all linear layers (attention q/k/v/o, FFN up/gate/down, embeddings optional per QuaRot convention — default: quantize weights, keep lm_head/embed in FP for the accuracy path, matching QuaRot's weight-only scheme).

## 4. Pinned environment (for reproducibility)
```
python: 3.11 (note: this sandbox is 3.14 with no ML stack; target env below)
torch==2.3.1            # CUDA 12.1 build
transformers==4.44.0    # Phi-3 supported
quarot: git+https://github.com/NeuronAI-Apps/QuaRot @ <pinned commit>  # pin a specific SHA
gptqmodel==1.4.1        # non-QuaRot GPTQ + RTN baseline
lm-evaluation-harness==0.4.5
datasets==2.20.0
```
- Pin the exact QuaRot commit at setup time (record SHA). Rationale: QuaRot API is still evolving; a SHA guarantees the rotation + GPTQ path is reproducible.
- **GPTQModel** for the non-QuaRot GPTQ/RTN baselines; **QuaRot's internal GPTQ** for QuaRot-GPTQ. Keeping the non-QuaRot GPTQ on one well-maintained implementation isolates QuaRot's effect.

## 5. Calibration (GPTQ paths only)
- **Set:** C4 (`allenai/c4`, "en", "2024_07_30" stream), **128 sequences × 2048 tokens**, seeded sampling.
- Used by: GPTQ (cell 2) and QuaRot-GPTQ (cell 4). RTN and QuaRot-RTN need no calibration (rounding / rotation-only).
- QuaRot additionally fits its rotation (Hadamard + learned/QR step) from the same calibration batch — record the rotation-fit parameters in the run manifest.

## 6. Evaluation protocol
### 6.1 Perplexity
- **Corpus:** WikiText-103 test split (`Salesforce/wikitext`, `wikitext-103-raw`), ~4.7M tokens.
- **Context:** **primary 2048** (parity with QuaRot paper; standard for cross-model comparison), **sensitivity 4096** (model max). Rationale: 2048 keeps the headline comparable to the source; 4096 checks whether Phi-3's longer context changes the conclusion.
- **Method:** standard sliding-window eval (stride = context, no overlap), sum log-loss / token count → exp for PPL. Identical pipeline for all 13 cells.
- Pseudocode: `ppl = exp(sum(loss_tokens)/num_tokens)` over the full test split, per (config, width, context).

### 6.2 Zero-shot accuracy (lm-eval-harness)
- **Tasks (5, zero-shot, no OBQA):** `hellaswag`, `piqa`, `arc_easy`, `arc_challenge`, `winogrande`.
- **Why:** standard quant-paper suite; broad, cheap, directly comparable to QuaRot's reported metrics.
- **Accuracy metric:** `acc_norm` for hellaswag/winogrande (standard), `acc` for piqa/arc.
- Report per-task acc and a macro average.

## 7. Controls
- **Unquantized reference (cell 0):** FP16/BF16 `Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct`, identical eval pipeline → the "no quantization" anchor.
- **Non-QuaRot RTN & GPTQ (cells 1–2)** at the same widths → baselines that isolate QuaRot's contribution.
- Same calibration, group size, tokenizer, and eval code across all cells; only the quantizer varies.
- Single-seed; report the seed. Deterministic rotation fit where possible.

## 8. Analysis plan
- **Primary metric — QuaRot delta per bit-width:**
  - Δ_RTN(b) = quality(QuaRot-RTN_b) − quality(RTN_b)
  - Δ_GPTQ(b) = quality(QuaRot-GPTQ_b) − quality(GPTQ_b)
  - for b ∈ {4,6,8}, quality = −PPL (higher better) and zero-shot acc (higher better).
  - This is the actual generalization signal: does QuaRot's relative gain over its plain counterpart hold on Phi-3 as it did on LLaMA?
- **Secondary:** absolute PPL/acc vs the FP reference (quantization tax), and RTN-vs-GPTQ gap under and without QuaRot.
- **6-bit interpolation check:** expect INT6 PPL/acc to lie between INT4 and INT8 (near-linear in the 4–8 range). A 6-bit point that *worsens* relative to interpolation, or that breaks monotonicity (e.g., 6-bit PPL > 4-bit PPL), indicates an implementation/codebook bug (mis-set number of levels, wrong clipping range, or a GPTQ 6-level Hessian-quantization defect) rather than a scientific result. Flag any such deviation before interpretation.
- **Presentation:** table of 13 cells × {PPL@2048, PPL@4096, 5-task acc, macro acc}; a small bar/line figure of Δ per bit-width; note where the 4096 sensitivity changes conclusions.
- **Statistical care:** single deterministic run per cell (standard in quant literature); if budget allows, repeat the zero-shot eval to report run-to-run stability, but no significance testing is required for a deterministic pipeline.

## 9. Feasibility assessment
- **Model size:** ~3.8B params. Weight bytes: FP16 ≈ 7.6 GB; INT8 ≈ 3.8 GB; INT6 ≈ 2.9 GB; INT4 ≈ 1.9 GB (plus small scale/zero-point overhead).
- **Per-cell VRAM estimate (inference + eval):**
  - FP16: ~8 GB weights + activations/eval buffer ≈ **12–16 GB**.
  - INT8: ~4 GB weights + dequant buffers ≈ **8–12 GB**.
  - INT6: ~3–4 GB + buffers ≈ **8–12 GB**.
  - INT4: ~2–3 GB + buffers ≈ **6–10 GB**.
  - **A single A100-80G is comfortably sufficient for all 13 cells** (largest cell ~16 GB). H100 also fine. Even a 24 GB card suffices for the quantized cells but is tight for FP16 eval at 4096 context.
- **GPTQ/QuaRot calibration cost:** GPTQ is Hessian-based and GPU-bound; calibration (128×2048) for a 3.8B model is on the order of minutes-to-low-hours per quantized cell on a modern GPU. QuaRot's rotation fit adds a comparable, one-time cost per width. Total across 12 quantized cells is well within a day on one A100/H100.
- **CPU-only fallback:** **NOT practical for GPTQ/QuaRot-GPTQ** (Hessian inversion/solver is prohibitively slow in CPU-only). RTN/QuaRot-RTN quantization is CPU-feasible, but **perplexity + zero-shot inference of a 3.8B model on CPU is impractically slow** for a full WikiText-103 + 5-task eval. Recommend GPU for the full matrix; if no GPU is available, restrict to a reduced token budget and RTN-only cells as a partial-feasibility probe.
- **This sandbox:** no GPU, no ML stack, network disabled — confirms this is a design-only deliverable; the above targets a separate GPU environment.

## 10. Assumptions & risks (flagged, not fixed requirements)
- **A1 — 6-bit is a design assumption.** QuaRot does not pin 6-bit group size/codebook; we use a 64-level symmetric codebook with g=128. If the intended comparison differs, the 6-bit column is the one to revisit.
- **A2 — Architecture transfer risk (key open risk).** Phi-3's GQA head layout and SwiGLU gates may not accept QuaRot's rotations without modification (QuaRot targets LLaMA-style attention/MLP). Mitigation: verify the QuaRot commit supports Phi-3's config (or apply rotations per head-group); if rotation application fails or degrades abnormally, report it as a *generalization limitation* rather than a bug — that is a valid answer to the question.
- **A3 — Library pinning.** Exact QuaRot SHA, GPTQModel version, and lm-eval-harness version must be fixed and recorded; QuaRot's API is still evolving, so a SHA is mandatory for reproducibility.
- **A4 — GPTQ 6-level support.** Confirm the chosen GPTQModel build supports arbitrary 6-level integer quantization; if not, 6-bit GPTQ cells fall back to the QuaRot implementation or are dropped and noted.
- **A5 — Checkpoint is instruct-tuned** (fixed by the question, not an assumption).
- **A6 — Hardware.** Feasibility assumes a single modern GPU (A100-80G/H100); CPU-only is not practical for the full matrix (see §9).

---
**Reproducibility manifest (record per run):** model id, QuaRot SHA, gptqmodel/lm-eval/torch/transformers versions, calibration set+seed, group size, bit-width, context length, per-task acc, PPL. No experiment was executed in producing this design.

## Инвентаризация входных данных
- `/workspace` содержит только `task.json` (вопрос + пометка «Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required»).
- Репо QuaRot, весов модели, датасетов в workspace нет. Среда: Python 3.14, **нет GPU**, **нет сети**, ML-стек (torch/transformers/lm-eval) не установлен.
- Вывод: это чисто дизайн-задача. Все детали setup опираются на публичные сведения о QuaRot (NeurIPS 2024) и репо MIT Han Lab QuaRot; критичные параметры сверим с разделами setup из твоих топиков (setup_1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 11), где я не уверен.

## Предлагаемый подход

**1. Экспериментальная сетка (13 конфигураций)**
- Модель: `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` (3.8B, bf16, ctx 4096, hidden 3072, GQA 32q/8kv, head_dim 96, RoPE, RMSNorm, SwiGLU).
- Методы: (a) FP16 baseline; (b) plain RTN; (c) plain GPTQ; (d) QuaRot-RTN; (e) QuaRot-GPTQ.
- Битность: 4, 6, 8 → по 2 метода × 3 биты × 2 варианта (с/без QuaRot) + FP16 = 13 точек.
- Ключевое решение: режим активаций. Предлагаю симметричный W{b}A{b} (W4A4 / W6A6 / W8A8, per-token dynamic quant активаций, group size 128 для весов) для всех методов — это воспроизводит W4A4-сравнение из статьи QuaRot, где базлайны тоже W4A4. Альтернатива (W-only для b>4) — отмечу как open question.
- Ключевые контрольные точки: **FP16 baseline** (да, обязательно) и **plain RTN/GPTQ без QuaRot** на каждой битности (да, обязательно — изолирует вклад QuaRot от самого квантования).

**2. Perplexity**
- Датасеты: WikiText2 (test, primary) + C4 (val, secondary) — как в статье QuaRot.
- Длина: чанки 2048 токенов (вписывается в 4K; left padding, без оверлепа); опционально добавить прогон при seq_len 4096 как стресс-тест 4k-варианта.
- Объём: WikiText2 test — все чанки (~300×2048), C4 — 1000 чанков (стандарт статьи).
- Batch size 8, bf16 inference, отчёт: ppl + bits-per-byte.

**3. Zero-shot accuracy**
- lm-eval-harness, 6 задач как в статье: hellaswag, piqa, winogrande, arc_easy, boolq, openbookqa; метрика accuracy, zero-shot, batch 8, фиксированный seed.

**4. Калибрация (GPTQ и QuaRot-GPTQ)**
- C4, 128 образцов × 2048 токенов (default статьи QuaRot), один общий seed для всех методов, чтобы сравнение было честным.

**5. Специфика QuaRot на Phi-3 (главные риски корректности)**
- hidden_dim 3072 и head_dim 96 — **не степени двойки**, а QuaRot строится на Hadamard-преобразованиях. Решение: блочный WHT (блоки по 32) или случайные ортогональные матрицы — нужно проверить, что поддерживает репо, и явно зафиксировать в дизайне.
- GQA + RoPE: ротации R применяются к q и k projection согласованно, до RoPE (механизм из статьи); отдельный sanity-check, что rotated FP16 ≈ исходный FP16 (инвариантность).
- Фиксация random seed для случайных знаков Hadamard-ротаций; опционально 3 сида для оценки дисперсии.

**6. Sanity-проверки (дешёвые контрольные точки)**
- QuaRot-FP16 (ротации без квантования) ≈ FP16 baseline по ppl.
- Монотонность: 8-bit ≥ 6-bit ≥ 4-bit по ppl/accuracy; 8-bit близок к FP16.
- Сравнение dequantized весов с оригиналом (max/mean error) — верификация пайплайна.

**7. Ресурсы (оценки для реальной машины, не для этой)**
- 1× GPU 24–40GB (A100/RTX 6000): bf16-модель ~7.6GB, GPTQ с Hessian по слоям — пик ~12–16GB; inference ~8–10GB.
- Время: offline-ротации весов ~10 мин/конфиг; GPTQ-калибровка ~15–40 мин/конфиг; ppl ~5–15 мин; 6 zero-shot задач ~1–2 ч. Итого **~12–24 GPU-ч** на 1 GPU. CPU-только прогон GPTQ/eval технически возможен, но нецелесообразен (дни вместо часов).

**8. Что прошу подтвердить по твоим топикам (setup_1/3/4/6/8/11)**
1. Режим активаций для 6/8-bit: W{b}A{b} или weights-only? (влияет на всю сетку)
2. Квантизация: стандартные INT с per-group scale или SPoW (signed power-of-2) коды? Вопрос говорит «INT4/6/8» → предлагаю стандартные INT, SPoW не используем.
3. Точные датасеты/объёмы ppl и размер калибрационного набора в статье (128×2048 C4 — верно?).
4. Поддерживает ли репо QuaRot Phi-3 из коробки (список моделей) и какой вариант Hadamard для не-степени-двойки размеров — если в топиках есть описание.

**Главные неопределённости (помимо вопросов выше)**
- Это instruct-модель (нет base-варианта 4k) → ppl будет выше, чем у base-моделей из статьи; сравниваем только внутри нашего эксперимента, а не с цифрами статьи.
- 6-bit — нестандартная битность, мало публичных референсов; интерпретируем как relative comparison внутри сетки.
- Один seed ротаций → возможная дисперсия; опциональное повторение с 3 сидами удваивает время на QuaRot-конфиги.
- Реальная запускательная машина (GPU + доступ к HF) отсутствует в этой среде — дизайн предполагает её наличие.

Жду подтверждения/правка по пунктам 8 и решения по W{b}A{b} — после этого соберу полный дизайн (stage=result) с точными командами/аргументами репо, таблицами результатов и критериями интерпретации.

# Экспериментный дизайн: обобщение QuaRot на Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct

**Статус: дизайн. Эксперимент НЕ выполнялся** — в текущей среде нет GPU, сети и ML-стека (проверено: `/workspace` содержит только `task.json`, `nvidia-smi` не работает, torch/transformers/lm-eval не установлены). Ниже — полный план для запуска на отдельной машине.

---

## 1. Обоснование ключевых решений

| Решение | Обоснование |
|---|---|
| Модель `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` (3.8B, bf16, ctx 4096, hidden 3072, GQA 32q/8kv, head_dim 96, RoPE, RMSNorm, SwiGLU) | Формулировка задачи. Это «non-LLAMA» модель, но архитектурно близка к LLaMA-2 (RMSNorm/SwiGLU/RoPE/GQA), поэтому QuaRot-механизм *должен* переноситься — именно это и проверяем. Отличия, требующие внимания: hidden 3072 и head_dim 96 не степени двойки (Hadamard), GQA 32:8. |
| Сетка: FP16 + {RTN, GPTQ} × {4,6,8} × {plain, QuaRot} = 13 конфигураций | Plain-базлайны изолируют вклад QuaRot от самого квантования; FP16 — общая точка отсчёта. 6-bit включён по задаче, хотя нестандартен (см. §4, caveat). |
| Режим активаций: **W{b}A{b} (primary)** — W4A4/W6A6/W8A8, per-token dynamic quant активаций | Точное соответствие W4A4-конвенции статьи QuaRot, где все сравнения (включая базлайны) идут в режиме W4A4; иначе QuaRot сравнивали бы с более «щадящим» W-only. Per-token dynamic — стандарт QuaRot (нет статических per-channel scale, которые и ломаются на аутлиерах). **Weights-only (W{b}A16) — secondary ablation** (6 доп. строк, §2.3), чтобы атрибутировать выигрыш именно ротациям, а не режиму активаций. |
| Стандартные симметричные INT с per-group scale, **group_size = 128** | Задача говорит «INT4/INT6/INT8» (не SPoW); group 128 — default репо/articles QuaRot; b=6 даёт 64 кодовые точки, b=8 — 256, всё равномерно покрывается standard INT. |
| GPTQ: Hessian-based, damp = 0.01 | Default GPTQ; единственный параметр, отличаемый от RTN, — использование Hessian, всё остальное идентично RTN, чтобы сравнение RTN vs GPTQ было чистым. |
| Калибрация: **C4, 128 образцов × 2048 токенов, seed 42**, общий для всех методов | Default статьи QuaRot; общий seed/набор гарантирует, что различия между методами — не от калибрации. 2048 < 4096, вписывается в контекст модели. |
| Rотации QuaRot: **block-WHT-32 (primary)** — Hadamard 32×32, тайлинг по 96 блоков на hidden 3072, по 3 блока на head_dim 96; случайные sign-flips, seed 42; весовые ротации W ← R·W (input side) и W ← W·Rᵀ (output side) применяются офлайн ко всем линейным слоям (q/k/v/o, fc1/fc2) | QuaRot требует ортогональные ротации размерности d; 3072/96 не степени двойки → блочный WHT сохраняет ортогональность и O(d log d). R на q и k применяется согласованно **до RoPE** (механизм статьи), что сохраняет rotary-инвариантность. **Fallback: случайные ортогональные матрицы (Гаусс + QR, тот же seed 42)** — если block-WHT-32 не проходит gate G1. |
| Perplexity: WikiText2 (test, primary) + C4 (val, secondary), чанки 2048, left padding, batch 8, bf16 inference | Те же датасеты, что в статье QuaRot → сопоставимый протокол; 2048 вписывается в 4K-контекст. WikiText2 test — все чанки (~300×2048), C4 — 1000 чанков (объём статьи). Отчёт: ppl + bits-per-byte (bpb). Опционально: прогон WikiText2 при seq_len 4096 как стресс-тест 4k-контекста (влияет только на порядок чанков, не на метрику первично). |
| Zero-shot: lm-eval-harness, 6 задач: **hellaswag, piqa, winogrande, arc_easy, boolq, openbookqa**, accuracy, num_fewshot=0, batch 8, seed 42 | Точный набор задач из статьи QuaRot → единый протокол; zero-shot по формулировке задачи. |
| Один фиксированный seed (42) везде: калб, ротации, eval | Воспроизводимость; дисперсия от случайных ротаций — единственная неконтролируемая случайность, за неё отвечает gate G1 + опциональное повторение 3 сидов (см. §5). |

---

## 2. Полная матрица конфигураций

### 2.1. Primary grid — 13 конфигураций

| ID | Метод | Битность (W/A) | QuaRot | Group | Rотации |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | FP16 baseline | 16/16 | — | — | — |
| C0r | **(gate)** QuaRot-FP16: только ротации, без квантования | 16/16 | да | — | block-WHT-32, seed 42 |
| C1 | RTN | 4/4 | нет | 128 | — |
| C2 | GPTQ (damp 0.01) | 4/4 | нет | 128 | — |
| C3 | QuaRot-RTN | 4/4 | да | 128 | block-WHT-32, seed 42 |
| C4 | QuaRot-GPTQ | 4/4 | да | 128 | block-WHT-32, seed 42 |
| C5–C8 | RTN / GPTQ / QuaRot-RTN / QuaRot-GPTQ | 6/6 | как в строке | 128 | как в строке |
| C9–C12 | RTN / GPTQ / QuaRot-RTN / QuaRot-GPTQ | 8/8 | как в строке | 128 | как в строке |

Единые гиперпараметры всех квантованных конфигураций:
- **Весовое квантование:** signed symmetric INT, per-group scale, `group_size = 128`.
- **Активации:** per-token dynamic quant, тот же `bits`, без сглаживания.
- **GPTQ:** `damp = 0.01`, sequential per-layer, калб = C4 128×2048, seed 42.
- **QuaRot:** block-WHT-32 (96 блоков на hidden 3072; 3 блока на head_dim 96), random sign-flips seed 42, q/k согласованно до RoPE, v и MLP-проекции — по стандартной схеме QuaRot; весовые ротации применяются офлайн, артефакт — ротированный checkpoint.
- **Inference:** bf16, dequant on-the-fly, `batch_size = 8`, `seq_len = 2048` (ppl), `seed = 42`.

### 2.2. Gate-конфигурация
C0r выполняется **первой** и является hard gate (G1, §3): до его прохождения ни одна квантованная конфигурация не запускается.

### 2.3. Secondary ablation (опционально, после primary grid)
A1–A6: те же 4 метода × {4,6,8}, но **W{b}A16** (weights-only). Назначение — атрибуция: если QuaRot-W{b}A16 ≈ plain-W{b}A16, а QuaRot-W{b}A{b} сильно лучше plain-W{b}A{b}, то выигрыш QuaRot — именно в защите активаций от аутлиеров.

---

## 3. Контрольные точки и sanity-проверки (pass/fail)

| Gate | Проверка | Критерий PASS | Действие при FAIL |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G1 (HARD, до любых квантованных прогонов)** | QuaRot-FP16 (C0r) vs FP16 (C0): ppl WikiText2 и ppl C4 + 6 zero-shot | \|Δppl\| ≤ **0.5** на обоих датасетах И Δaccuracy ≤ **1.0 п.п.** на каждой из 6 задач | Перейти на fallback — случайные ортогональные матрицы (seed 42), повторить gate. Если снова FAIL — **стоп**, отладка ротаций (подозрение: RoPE/GQA-интеракция или тайлинг блоков) |
| G2 | Декуантованные веса C9 (QuaRot-RTN 8-bit) vs FP16: relative L2 error по слоям | < 2% для всех linear-слоёв; конечный и ненулевой (квантование реально применяется) | Отладка пайплайна квантизации |
| G3 | Монотонность битности внутри каждого метода: ppl(8) ≤ ppl(6) ≤ ppl(4) | Выполняется с допуском 0.1 ppl | Не фатально — флагаем как наблюдение и разбираем (кандидат: 6-bit caveat, §4) |
| G4 | QuaRot-8bit (C11/C12) vs FP16 | Δppl(WikiText2) ≤ 1.0 (ожидаемое near-lossless) | Не фатально; пересмотр интерпретации 8-bit |
| G5 | Пиковая GPU-память и время на конфиг | ≤ 24GB; ≤ 3 ч на конфиг | Уменьшить batch до 4 / chunk калба |

Примечание: G1 — единственный hard gate; G2 блокирует запуск eval-фазы (но не квантизацию); G3–G5 — информационные.

---

## 4. План анализа

**Формат результата:** одна таблица 13 строк × 8 метрик: ppl_WT2, ppl_C4, bpb_WT2, acc(hellaswag, piqa, winogrande, arc_easy, boolq, openbookqa).

**Вопрос 1 — обобщается ли QuaRot (главный):**
- Δppl и Δacc для пар (C3 vs C1, C4 vs C2) на 4-bit; аналогично на 6/8-bit.
- **Критерий хорошего обобщения (все три):**
  1. На 4-bit (где plain-методы деградируют сильнее всего) QuaRot-RTN/GPTQ дают Δppl ≥ 0 в пользу QuaRot, а ppl QuaRot-4bit в пределах ~1–2 от FP16;
  2. Zero-shot: Δacc ≤ 1 п.п. от FP16 на ≥ 5 из 6 задач для QuaRot-4bit;
  3. На 6/8-bit QuaRot **не ухудшает** ни одну конфигурацию относительно plain-аналога (нет регрессий за пределами CI).
- Значимость: для Δaccuracy — Wilson 95% CI на разность долей (N задач у каждой метрики в lm-eval: hellaswag 7982, piqa 3084, winogrande 1267, arc_easy 2376, boolq 943, openbookqa 500); Δ внутри CI считаем ничьей. Для ppl — сравнение на одних и тех же чанках (детерминированно, CI не нужен).
- Если пункт 1 не выполняется на 4-bit, но выполняется на 8-bit — вывод: «QuaRot переносится, но его преимущество на Phi-3 меньше, чем на LLaMA» (т.е. аутлиер-структура активаций Phi-3 мягче) — это тоже валидный ответ на вопрос.

**Вопрос 2 — RTN vs GPTQ внутри QuaRot:**
- C3 vs C4 (и C5–C8, C9–C12 по битностям): ожидаем GPTQ ≤ RTN по ppl (Hessian-компенсация). Ключевой вопрос: сохраняется ли разрыв при росте битности (на 8-bit разрыв должен сокращаться — проверка на соответствие ожидаемой физике).
- Отдельно: RTN vs GPTQ в plain-режиме (C1 vs C2 и т.д.) — если QuaRot меняет иерархию RTN/GPTQ, это самостоятельное наблюдение.

**Caveat 6-bit (обязательная пометка в отчёте):** 6-bit — нестандартная битность без публичных референсов; интерпретируется **только relatively** внутри нашей сетки (ожидаемо между 4 и 8). Нарушение монотонности G3 на 6-bit не опровергает дизайн — помечается как наблюдение.

**Caveat instruct-model perplexity (обязательная пометка в отчёте):** Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct — instruction-tuned модель, base-варианта 4k не существует. **Абсолютные значения ppl НЕ сопоставимы** с цифрами статьи QuaRot (там base-модели LLaMA/Mistral/OPT) и будут системно выше. Все выводы строятся исключительно на **внутриэкспериментальных дельтах** (QuaRot vs plain, б vs б, vs FP16). Zero-shot accuracy этой оговорки не подвержены.

**Опциональная робастность:** повтор 4 QuaRot-4bit конфигураций (C3, C4 и plain-аналоги — нет, только C3/C4) с 3 разными сидами ротаций (42/43/44) → оценка дисперсии Hadamard-ротаций; удвоение времени только на 2 конфигурации (~+2–3 GPU-ч).

**Реестр воспроизводимости:** git-хэши QuaRot/transformers/lm-eval-harness, точные версии, все CLI-аргументы каждого конфига, сырые JSON/CSV выходов — в одном run-каталоге.

---

## 5. Feasibility: железо, софт, время

**Железо (для реальной машины, не для этой среды):**
- **GPU: 1× 24GB минимально, 40GB комфортно.** Бюджет: bf16-модель ~7.6GB; пик GPTQ (Hessian по слоям + калб-активации) ~12–16GB; inference ~8–10GB. Multi-GPU не требуется.
- **CPU/RAM:** 32GB RAM, ≥ 16 ядер (калб и eval — GPU-bound, CPU для токенизации).
- **Диск: ~100GB** — FP16 checkpoint 7.6GB + 13 квантованных артефактов (~1.9–7.6GB каждый) + C4/WikiText2 (~десятки МБ) + данные lm-eval (~1–2GB) + логи.
- **Сеть:** нужен доступ к HuggingFace (модель, датасеты) и git (QuaRot, lm-eval-harness).

**Софт:** Python 3.10–3.12 (не 3.14 как в этой среде — torch/transformers пока нестабильны на 3.14), torch (CUDA), transformers ≥ 4.37 (поддержка Phi-3), QuaRot repo (git clone), lm-eval-harness, datasets, accelerate.

**Оценка времени на 1 GPU (оценки, не замеры):**
| Этап | На конфиг |
|---|---|
| QuaRot offline-ротации весов (только C0r, C3, C4, C7, C8, C11, C12) | ~10 мин |
| GPTQ-калб 128×2048 (C2, C4, C6, C8, C10, C12) | ~15–40 мин |
| Perplexity (WT2 ~300 чанков + C4 1000 чанков) | ~5–15 мин |
| Zero-shot, 6 задач, batch 8 | ~1–2 ч |

- **Primary grid (13 конфигов): ~12–24 GPU-ч** (доминирует zero-shot eval).
- Secondary ablation (6 конфигов): + ~8–12 GPU-ч.
- Опциональные 3 сида: + ~2–3 GPU-ч.
- Итого с аблацией и сидами: **~25–40 GPU-ч**, т.е. < 2 дней на одной A100; без опций — ~1 день.
- Риски: (а) репо QuaRot может не поддерживать Phi-3 из коробки → потребуется добавить конфиг модели (1–2 дня инженерной работы, вне GPU-бюджета); (б) block-WHT-32 потребует fallback (покрывается G1, +~2 GPU-ч на перегон); (в) 6-bit-путь GPTQ в репо — проверить до старта (dry-run на 1 слое).

**Порядок запуска:** C0 → C0r (gate G1) → C9/C10/C11/C12 (8-bit, проверка G2/G4) → C5–C8 → C1–C4 (4-bit, главная зона интереса) → eval-фаза по мере готовности → ablation A1–A6 → опциональный 3-сид прогон.

2) PROPUESTA DE ENFOQUE (esqueleto): modelo microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (~3.8B) vía transformers + pipeline QuaRot (Hadamard + cuantización de pesos/activaciones/KV). C4) y zero-shot accuracy (ARC-e, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, BoolQ vía lm-evaluation-harness). Un solo set de calibración (C4 ~128 muestras, seq-len ~2048, por confirmar con el paper). 3) SUPUESTOS E INCERTIDUMBRES: (a) Phi-3 no está en la lista oficial de modelos de QuaRot (paper: Llama-2) → es la pregunta central; riesgos: GQA, sin bias, proyección qkv fusionada, formato chat; (b) 6-bit puede no estar soportado por GPTQ estándar ({2,3,4,8}) → celda GPTQ-6bit podría ser N/A; (c) datasets/calibración exactos del paper no confirmados localmente — propongo WikiText-2 + C4 + 5 tareas, o pedir aclaración por topics (presupuesto: 6 preguntas); (d) sin GPU/red/deps aquí: ejecución local imposible; GPTQ requiere CUDA, así que bajo "sin GPU" el diseño debe declararse design-only (como indica track.md) o degradarse; (e) modelo instruct vs base: ppl en texto crudo sobre modelo chat puede estar sesgada; (f) zero-shot reportado por-tarea + macro-average. payload.answer:
# DISEÑO FINAL — ¿Cómo generaliza QuaRot a Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct? (design-only)

## 0. Declaración de estado
Este documento es **solo un diseño**. No se ha ejecutado ningún comando de experimento, cuantización ni evaluación; no existen resultados numéricos. Se verificó únicamente el entorno (ver §7).

## 1. Requisitos fijos (no negociables, por la pregunta)
- Modelo: `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` (~3.8B, GQA, sin bias, proyección `qkv` fusionada, formato de chat).
- Precisions: **INT4, INT6, INT8**.
- Métodos: **QuaRot-RTN** y **QuaRot-GPTQ** (i.e., cuantización RTN/GPTQ aplicada *después* de aplicar las rotaciones de Hadamard de QuaRot a pesos, activaciones y KV-cache).

## 2. Diseño de la rejilla
| ID | Método | Bits | Rol |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP16 | sin cuantizar | — | Referencia/control |
| Q-RTN-4 / Q-RTN-6 / Q-RTN-8 | QuaRot-RTN | 4/6/8 | Tratamiento (obligatorio) |
| Q-GPTQ-4 / Q-GPTQ-6 / Q-GPTQ-8 | QuaRot-GPTQ | 4/6/8 | Tratamiento (obligatorio, salvo N/A en §3) |
| B-RTN-4 / B-RTN-6 / B-RTN-8 | RTN plano (sin QuaRot) | 4/6/8 | **Opcional** — control (ver §2.1) |
| B-GPTQ-4 / B-GPTQ-6 / B-GPTQ-8 | GPTQ plano (sin QuaRot) | 4/6/8 | **Opcional** — control (ver §2.1) |

**§2.1 Baselines sin QuaRot (opcionales, no obligatorios):** se incluyen **únicamente como control para aislar el efecto de las rotaciones de Hadamard**: con ellos el delta (QuaRot − plano) a cada bit mide específicamente la contribución de la rotación, separada de la contribución del algoritmo RTN/GPTQ. Si el presupuesto de GPU-horas es ajustado, se recortan primero (prioridad: rejilla obligatoria 2×3 + FP16).

**§3 Criterio GPTQ-6bit (documentado explícitamente):** GPTQ estándar (autogptq/GPTQModel) soporta típicamente bits ∈ {2, 3, 4, 8}; el 6-bit es nativo en el pathway de cuantización de QuaRot pero no está garantizado en su módulo GPTQ. **Criterio operativo:** (1) en el smoke test (§6), intentar cuantizar una capa con QuaRot-GPTQ a 6-bit; (2) si el pathway lo soporta, incluir Q-GPTQ-6 como celda normal; (3) si lanza error/soporte ausente, **marcar la celda Q-GPTQ-6 como N/A con la justificación registrada** (mensaje de error, versión del código), **sin imputar ni inventar ningún valor**. Lo mismo aplica simétricamente a B-GPTQ-6.

## 3. Protocolo de cuantización
- Carga: `transformers` + pipeline de QuaRot (rotaciones de Hadamard aplicadas una vez de forma estática; cuantización per-channel de pesos, per-token de activaciones, KV-cache según config de QuaRot).
- **Set de calibración único y compartido** por TODAS las celdas (RTN y GPTQ, con y sin QuaRot): C4, 128 muestras, seq-len 2048, seed fija. (Valores por confirmar contra el setup del paper vía topics; si el paper difiere, prevalece el paper.)
- Parámetros por bit: group_size estándar de QuaRot (128) para GPTQ; RTN sin calibración dependiente más allá de la misma data.
- Modelos cuantizados se guardan a disco para que la evaluación sea reproducible y separable de la cuantización.

## 4. Métricas y evaluación
**Perplexity:**
- WikiText-2 (test split) como métrica principal; C4 test como secundario. Mismo protocolo de tokenización, padding y longitud de ventana (2048) para todas las celdas.
- **Sesgo instruct (justificación, §4.1):** Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct fue afinado con RLHF/SFT en formato de chat; su distribución de entrenamiento está condicionada al template de chat (tokens de sistema/usuario/asistente). Evaluar perplexity sobre WikiText-2 *crudo* (sin template) mide fuera de la distribución de entrenamiento del modelo → la ppl absoluta puede estar inflada respecto a un modelo base, y la degradación por cuantización puede verse distorsionada (p. ej., si las rotaciones alteran la coherencia del formato de chat, o si el modelo penaliza texto sin estructura de chat). **Mitigación doble:** (a) reportar ppl en dos condiciones: *raw* (sin template) y *templated* (cada segmento envuelto en el chat template de Phi-3), con raw como número principal por comparabilidad con el paper (modelos base) y templated como robustez; (b) **declarar explícitamente como limitación** en el reporte final: la ppl en texto crudo sobre un modelo instruct no es una medida "limpia" de calidad intrínseca, y las conclusiones sobre generalización de QuaRot deberían leerse como comparaciones *relativas* (delta vs FP16 del mismo modelo), no absolutas.
- **Zero-shot accuracy:** ARC-e, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, BoolQ, vía `lm-evaluation-harness` (misma versión, mismo prompt template, `num_fewshot=0`) para todas las celdas. Reporte **por tarea + promedio macro**. (Lista por confirmar contra el setup del paper.)

## 5. Controles
1. FP16/BF16 no cuantizado como referencia de cada métrica.
2. Mismo set de calibración para todos los métodos (elimina la varianza de calibración).
3. Mismo harness de evaluación y templates para todas las celdas.
4. Seeds fijas (calibración, inicialización, sampling en evals generativos) y versión de software pinneada (transformers, QuaRot, GPTQ lib, lm-eval) registrada en el diseño.
5. Smoke test de 1 capa/1 bit antes de lanzar la rejilla completa (valida el punto crítico de soporte de Phi-3, §6).
6. (Si presupuesto lo permite) ≥2 seeds de calibración para las celdas principales, reportando desviación entre seeds.

## 6. Plan de análisis
1. Tabla principal: métrica × (método × bits), con Δ vs FP16 (puntos absolutos para ppl y accuracy).
2. Pregunta 1 (generalización): ¿QuaRot-RTN/GPTQ en Phi-3 degrada menos que el esperado de LLaMA? Se responde con Δ vs FP16 y, si hay baselines, con la comparación cruzada.
3. Pregunta 2 (RTN vs GPTQ): comparación directa a cada bit (¿GPTQ compensa su costo de calibración en Phi-3?).
4. Pregunta 3 (efecto Hadamard, solo si hay baselines): Δ(QuaRot − plano) por bit.
5. Tendencia con bits: ¿la brecha RTN-vs-GPTQ y el beneficio de QuaRot crecen/decrecen al bajar de 8→4 bits?
6. Celdas N/A (p. ej. GPTQ-6bit) listadas aparte con justificación; no se incluyen en promedios.
7. Limitaciones declaradas: instruct-vs-base (§4.1), n=1 seed si aplica, un solo modelo (no se puede extrapolar a otros non-LLaMA).

## 7. Viabilidad y presupuesto de ejecución (ESPECIFICADO)
**Presupuesto especificado para la ejecución (fuera de este entorno):** **1 GPU externa, 24–80 GB** (A100 80GB o 4090 24GB; Phi-3-mini cuantizado cabe con holgura; cuantización GPTQ de 3.8B ≈ horas por celda; evals zero-shot de 5 tareas × ~13 celdas ≈ 1–2 días GPU en total, estimación del diseño, no medida).
**En ESTE entorno NO se ejecuta nada, y es inejecutable:** verificado Python 3.14.4 sin torch/transformers/datasets, sin caché HuggingFace (sin pesos), red desactivada (DNS falla → imposibles descargas), `gpu_enabled: false`. Adicionalmente, **GPTQ requiere CUDA** (autogptq/GPTQModel no tienen pathway CPU), por lo que la celda GPTQ es literalmente inejecutable sin GPU. El workspace contiene solo `task.json` y `track.md` dice "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required". RAM/CPU locales (2 TB RAM, 224 CPUs) serían suficientes para inferencia RTN en CPU, pero no hay modelo ni dependencias para intentarlo, y el brief lo prohíbe implícitamente.

## 8. Riesgos y supuestos
- **Soporte de Phi-3 en QuaRot (riesgo principal):** el paper evalúa Llama-2; Phi-3 no está documentado. Mitigación: smoke test de 1 capa antes de la rejilla; si falla, el experimento *es* la respuesta (documentar qué patch es necesario — eso mismo responde "cómo generaliza").
- GPTQ-6bit: criterio N/A documentado (§3).
- Datasets/calibración/tareas: valores propuestos (WikiText-2, C4 128×2048, 5 tareas) son propuestos por mí, **pendientes de confirmar** contra los setup del paper (topics disponibles); si el researcher confirma otros, se sustituyen sin cambiar la estructura.
- Supuesto: el entregable evaluado es este diseño (no una ejecución), conforme a `task.json`/`track.md`.

以下为初步检查与方案框架（纯设计任务，未运行任何实验）。

## 一、输入与仓库检查结果

对 /workspace 的完整排查结果：**不存在**任何相关脚本、配置或数据。

- `/workspace` 下仅有 `task.json` 一个文件（499 字节），内容为：任务问题（QuaRot 在 Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct 上的泛化性）、context（"Design an experiment... Do not claim that an experiment was run"）、`documents.track.md`（"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"）。
- 无 QuaRot 量化实现代码、无 Phi-3 模型权重/checkpoint、无 perplexity 计算脚本、无 zero-shot 评估脚本或基准数据集文件。
- 系统级检查：未发现 quarot/phi 相关目录；Python 3.14.4，torch / transformers / quarot / lm-eval 均未安装；网络禁用、无 GPU。

**结论**：本设计只能基于文档级规格（QuaRot 论文/仓库、lm-eval-harness、HF Hub 模型卡）编写，所有代码级细节（如 INT6 是否被量化函数原生支持）均无法在本地验证，只能列为假设/待确认项，并在设计中写明"执行前验证步骤"。

## 二、初步方案框架（全因子设计 + 分层对照）

**被试单元**：Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct（HF Transformers 格式，decoder-only，hidden 3072 / 32 层 / GQA，4K 上下文）。

**因子与条件**：
- 因子 A（量化方法，2 水平）：QuaRot-RTN、QuaRot-GPTQ
- 因子 B（精度，3 水平）：INT4、INT6、INT8
- → 2×3 全因子 = **6 个量化条件**，保证可估计方法×位宽交互效应

**对照组**：
- C1（主对照）：**FP16 未量化模型**，作为所有条件的参考上界，同时其指标本身即"零量化损失"基线；
- C2（机制对照，建议保留）：**无旋转的 vanilla RTN**（同位宽、同量化范围，仅去掉 incoherent processing），用于把 QuaRot 的收益分解为"旋转带来的收益"与"位宽带来的损失"，这也是 QuaRot 论文自身的对照方式；
- （可选 C3：无旋转 GPTQ，若算力允许，进一步隔离 GPTQ 误差补偿与旋转的交互。）

## 三、关键假设与不确定性

**主要假设**：
1. **INT6 支持**：假设 QuaRot 的 vector-wise 量化函数支持任意位宽（论文主要报告 4/6-bit），INT6 对 RTN 与 GPTQ 均可用；INT8 非论文重点，假设同样可行但缺乏论文直接依据。

5. **算力可行性**：3.8B 模型 FP16 约 7.6GB，7~9 个条件各自的校准+评估在单张 A100/H100 上可行（本任务不要求执行，仅作为设计合理性说明）。

# 完整实验设计：QuaRot 在 Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct 上的泛化性评估
（纯设计文档；未运行任何实验。所有"拟沿用/假设"参数均已标注依据，执行前须经第 8 节验证清单确认。）

## 1. 研究问题
- **RQ1（主）**：QuaRot 量化在 Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct 上的损失（perplexity 增量、zero-shot 掉点）与其在 LLaMA 上（论文已报告）相比处于什么水平？即 QuaRot 的 incoherent processing 是否泛化到非 LLaMA 架构。
- **RQ2**：在 4/6/8-bit 下，QuaRot-GPTQ 相对 QuaRot-RTN 的优势幅度如何随位宽变化？
- **RQ3（辅助）**：损失中多少来自位宽本身、多少可通过旋转避免？（由无旋转对照条件回答）

## 2. 模型与对象
- 模型：`microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct`（HF Transformers 格式，decoder-only，3.8B，hidden 3072，32 层，GQA 32Q/8KV，SwiGLU，RMSNorm，RoPE，4K 上下文）。
- 量化范围：attention 的 q/k/v/o 投影 + MLP 的 gate/up/down 投影；**embed_tokens 与 lm_head 保持 FP16**（依据：QuaRot 论文默认不量化 embedding/输出层）。
- 旋转：权重与激活两侧施加固定随机 Hadamard 变换（incoherent processing），无学习成分。

## 3. 实验设计结构（全因子 + 分层对照）
因子：方法 M ∈ {QuaRot-RTN, QuaRot-GPTQ, RTN-norot}，位宽 B ∈ {INT4, INT6, INT8}，另加 FP16 基线。

| 条件 ID | 方法 | 位宽 | 角色 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | FP16（不量化） | — | 主对照/参考上界 |
| Q1–Q3 | QuaRot-RTN | 4/6/8 | 处理组（2×3 全因子） |
| Q4–Q6 | QuaRot-GPTQ | 4/6/8 | 处理组（2×3 全因子） |
| R1–R3 | RTN-norot（同位宽、同量化范围，仅去除旋转） | 4/6/8 | 机制对照（RQ3） |
| G1（可选） | GPTQ-norot | INT4 | 仅当算力允许，隔离"GPTQ 补偿 × 旋转"交互 |

核心 10 条件（C0 + 9）；可选扩展至 11。无旋转 RTN 条件无需校准数据、确定性运行，边际成本低，故保留全三位宽。

## 4. 各条件方法细节（设计假设，见第 7 节）
- **QuaRot-RTN**：旋转后对权重按输出通道、激活按 token 做 symmetric vector-wise 量化（group = 完整向量，不分块），round-to-nearest。
- **QuaRot-GPTQ**：旋转后执行 GPTQ 逐列误差补偿；**group size 128**；percdamp=0.01、dampening=1e-2、block size 128、actorder 开启（GPTQ 默认，按 QuaRot 仓库实现为准）。
- **RTN-norot**：与 Q1–Q3 完全相同的量化范围/对称性/位宽，但不施加任何旋转（即 QuaRot 论文中的 vanilla RTN 对照）。
- **C0**：原始 FP16 权重，无任何变换。

## 5. 校准数据
- 来源：C4（en，validation split）；**128 条 × 4096 token**，固定随机种子（依据：QuaRot 论文校准配置）。
- 用途：仅 GPTQ 系条件（Q4–Q6、G1）需要；RTN 系与 FP16 为确定性流程。
- 说明：QuaRot 的旋转为固定随机 Hadamard，不依赖激活统计学习，因此校准数据不用于"拟合旋转"。

## 6. 评估指标与协议
### 6.1 Perplexity
- 语料：**WikiText-2 (test)** 与 **C4 (validation，取前 250 条)**（依据：论文评测口径；250 条为常用子集，若论文口径不同以代码验证为准）。
- 协议：模型自带 tokenizer；**上下文长度 4096**（匹配 Phi-3 的 4K）；左 padding、分块推理；ppl = exp(平均 cross-entropy)。
### 6.2 Zero-shot accuracy
- 工具：lm-eval-harness。
- 任务（7 个，与 QuaRot 论文 Table 2 完全一致，保证与 LLaMA 结果可比）：**PiQA、BoolQ、ARC-e、ARC-c、HellaSwag、WinoGrande、OpenBookQA**。
- **模板**：Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct 为 instruct 模型，**所有条件（含 C0）统一使用 Phi-3 chat template**（lm-eval-harness 的 Phi 模板），否则系统性低估。
- 报告：每任务 accuracy + 7 任务宏平均；另报告 4K 上下文内的最大生成长度限制（按任务默认）。
### 6.3 重复与随机性
- 单一随机种子（固定）保证可复现；RTN/FP16 条件确定性。
- 可选：对 Q1、Q4（INT4 两条件）各重复 3 个 GPTQ 种子，估计方差（RTN 重复无意义，因确定性）。

## 7. 设计假设（6 项，均非阻塞，逐条注明依据）
| # | 假设 | 依据 |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | 量化为对称；RTN 为 vector-wise（group=全向量）；GPTQ 为 grouped，group size 128 | QuaRot 论文核心即 vector-wise 量化；group 128 为 GPTQ 标准默认 |
| A2 | 校准数据 = C4 validation，128 条 × 4096 token，固定种子 | QuaRot 论文校准配置（128 样本、4096 上下文） |
| A3 | PPL 协议 = WikiText-2 test + C4 validation 子集，ctx=4096，左 padding | 论文评测口径；4096 匹配 Phi-3 4K 上下文 |
| A4 | Zero-shot = 论文同款 7 任务 + Phi-3 chat template | 与论文可比；instruct 模型必须用 chat 模板 |
| A5 | GPTQ 超参 = percdamp 0.01、damp 1e-2、block 128、actorder on | GPTQ 原始默认值，QuaRot 仓库沿用（执行前读代码确认） |
| A6 | INT8 视为一等条件（非仅对照） | 任务明确要求 4/6/8 三档；vector-wise 量化可平凡扩展到 8-bit；8-bit 结果作为"近无损"参考点。注：论文重点为 4/6-bit，8-bit 解读时不与论文直接对照 |

补充假设：A7 — QuaRot 量化函数原生支持 INT6/INT8（论文报告过 6-bit；本地无代码可验证，列入执行前检查）；A8 — 固定随机 Hadamard 旋转可直接平移到 GQA 的 k/v 投影（结构同构，需代码适配验证）。

## 8. 执行前验证清单（代码级，因本沙箱无 QuaRot 代码/模型/网络）
1. **位宽支持**：检查 QuaRot `quantize()` 函数签名，对小型 Linear 层跑 4/6/8-bit 单元测试，确认 INT6/INT8 原生可用；若 INT6 缺失，退化方案为直接调用底层量化核实现。
2. **模型适配**：确认 QuaRot 仓库（llama 专用模块）能否加载 Phi-3；预期需新增 Phi-3 模型包装类（RMSNorm/SwiGLU/GQA/RoPE 钩子）。验收标准：关闭旋转的 QuaRot 前向与原版 HF 模型逐层输出一致（数值容差 1e-3）。
3. **GQA 处理**：确认 k/v 投影（8 KV 头）旋转与量化路径与 q 一致；对照论文/issue 确认无特殊处理。
4. **模板验证**：用 3 条手工 prompt 验证 Phi-3 chat 模板在 lm-eval-harness 下输出格式正确，再跑 1 个任务的小样本。
5. **基线 sanity check**：C0 的 WikiText-2 ppl 与 7 任务 accuracy 应与社区公开值量级一致，否则排查 tokenizer/模板问题。
6. **资源检查**：3.8B FP16 ≈ 7.6GB；量化过程需同时持有旋转中间副本，预估峰值 < 24GB → 单张 A100/H100 足够。

## 9. 分析计划
1. 主结果表：10 条件 × {WT2 ppl, C4 ppl, 7 任务 acc, 宏平均 acc}。
2. **RQ1**：计算 Phi-3 上各 QuaRot 条件相对 C0 的损失，与论文 LLaMA 同位宽损失并列对比（描述性对比；单种子不做显著性检验，报告任务级掉点范围）。
3. **RQ2**：同位宽内 Q4–Q6 vs Q1–Q3 的差值序列，观察"位宽越低 GPTQ 优势越大"的单调趋势。
4. **RQ3**：Q1–Q3 vs R1–R3 差值 = 旋转的净贡献（同位宽、同为 RTN，唯一差异是旋转）。
5. 判据（预期而非结果）：8-bit 条件 ppl 增量应接近 0；4-bit QuaRot 损失的量级若与 LLaMA 论文结果同阶，则支持"泛化良好"结论；若显著更大，进一步归因（R1–R3 对照可区分是架构对位宽更敏感，还是旋转在 Phi-3 上失效）。

## 10. 风险与缓解
| 风险 | 缓解 |
|---|---|
| INT6 不被原生支持 | 验证清单 #1；必要时手写 6-bit 量化核（对称、全向量），并在结果中注明 |
| QuaRot 仓库无 Phi-3 支持 | 适配工作包（清单 #2），以"关旋转=原版"为验收门 |
| instruct 模板错配导致 zero-shot 系统性偏低 | 所有条件统一模板 + 清单 #4 手工验证 |
| 单种子、无重复 → 无法做统计检验 | 明确声明描述性结论；可选 3 种子（INT4）补方差 |
| 数据集/模型需联网下载 | 执行环境预下载 C4、WikiText-2、7 个 zero-shot 数据集与模型权重（本沙箱网络禁用，属执行环境前提） |

## 11. 算力与工期估算（单卡 A100/H100）
- GPTQ 条件校准：各约 10–30 min；RTN/FP16：秒级。
- 每条件 PPL（2 语料 × 4K ctx）：约 5–15 min；zero-shot 7 任务：约 30–60 min。
- 10–11 条件合计约 **1–2 GPU-day**，含调试缓冲建议预留 3 天。

## 12. 交付物
1. 条件矩阵表（上表）与逐条件参数配置（YAML/JSON）；
2. 每条件原始日志（校准统计、ppl 分块明细、任务级 acc）；
3. 汇总结果表 + RQ1–RQ3 分析脚本与结论报告；
4. Phi-3 适配代码 diff 与"关旋转=原版"验收记录。

## 13. 局限性声明
- 单模型（Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct），结论不外推到其他非 LLaMA 架构；
- instruct 模型的 zero-shot 模板选择可能引入与论文（base 模型）不完全同质的比较；

payload.answer:
**1) Workspace inspection**

`/workspace` contains a single file: `task.json` (8 KB). It restates the task (design-only; "repositories and compute are not required") and contains no code. There is **no QuaRot code, no configuration files, no evaluation scripts, and no datasets** in the workspace. The sandbox is a bubblewrap environment with network disabled, GPU disabled, system Python with no project dependencies, and ~224 CPU cores. Consequence: the design must be written from the QuaRot paper's known setup, and the feasibility section must assume an external execution environment (GPU + QuaRot repo + datasets) rather than this sandbox.

**2) High-level approach (outline)**

*Design: a factorial sweep on a fixed model (Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, bf16).*

- **Conditions (19 total):**
  - Reference: unquantized bf16.
  - Plain (no rotations): RTN and GPTQ at 4/6/8-bit → 6 conditions.
  - QuaRot (Hadamard rotations + smoothing): RTN and GPTQ at 4/6/8-bit → 6 conditions.
  - Plus a "rotation-only" sanity condition (rotated but unquantized) as an implementation control.
- **Baselines:** unquantized Phi-3-mini is the anchor; plain RTN/GPTQ without rotations isolates the contribution of the rotation from the RTN-vs-GPTQ comparison. This gives both answers: RTN-vs-GPTQ *within* QuaRot (the literal question) and QuaRot-vs-plain (the generalization claim).
- **Bit-width semantics (needs a decision, see 3d):** I propose treating the sweep as *weight* bit-width with a fixed activation policy per condition — e.g., weight-only (W{n}A16) as the primary axis, with QuaRot's full W4A4/W8A8 mode as an additional arm at 4/8-bit if budget allows.
- **INT6 handling:** QuaRot's released pipeline natively supports 4-bit and 8-bit (its activation quantizers use residual decomposition: 4-bit = 2×2-bit, 8-bit = 2×4-bit sub-quantizers). 6-bit is **not native** to QuaRot. I would specify an explicit adaptation: a symmetric 6-bit weight quantizer (NF6-style, as in bitsandbytes) applied to the *rotated* weights, with activations kept at bf16 for the 6-bit condition (W6A16); optionally a 4+2-bit residual activation decomposition as a sensitivity check. This is a design adaptation, not a framework default.
- **Calibration:** one fixed calibration set (e.g., 512 sequences of 2048 tokens from C4/Pile, fixed seed) shared by all GPTQ and QuaRot runs so method comparisons are not confounded by calibration sampling.
- **Evaluation protocol:**
  - Perplexity: WikiText-2 (primary), C4 (secondary), optionally CPG — matching the QuaRot paper's set for comparability.
  - Zero-shot accuracy: lm-evaluation-harness with fixed prompt templates on HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-e, ARC-c, BoolQ, OBQA (the paper's suite).
  - Fixed seeds everywhere (RTN rounding, GPTQ, harness); identical tokenization/decoding across all conditions.
- **Controls:** (i) unquantized reference; (ii) rotation-only condition — Hadamard rotations are orthogonal, so unquantized perplexity should be ~invariant, validating the ported rotation implementation; (iii) optionally, reproduce one published QuaRot result (e.g., LLaMA-2-7B W4A4) before touching Phi-3 to validate the pipeline port.
- **Analysis plan (sketch):** report per-condition PPL and zero-shot accuracy; primary metric = delta from unquantized (ΔPPL, Δacc); primary contrast = QuaRot-GPTQ vs QuaRot-RTN at each bit-width; secondary contrast = QuaRot vs plain at each method×bit-width; bootstrap CIs on deltas; pre-registered "success" criteria (e.g., QuaRot degradation within a small margin of plain GPTQ, and GPTQ ≥ RTN under QuaRot).

**3) Consequential assumptions and uncertainties**

- **(a) INT6:** Not supported natively in QuaRot as far as I know — the design must specify the adaptation (6-bit weight quantizer on rotated weights; activation policy TBD). If your source-backed setup topics confirm different native support, the 6-bit arm changes materially.
- **(b) Datasets:** I default to the QuaRot paper's evaluation set (WikiText-2, C4, CPG; HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-e/c, BoolQ, OBQA) for direct comparability with published numbers. I have no strong preference beyond comparability — happy to take your guidance. Two caveats: Phi-3-mini is 4k-context (calibration/eval sequences should respect that) and instruct-tuned, so WikiText-2 PPL measures quantization *degradation* relative to its bf16 self more than absolute quality.
- **(c) QuaRot-free baselines:** I recommend *including* plain RTN/GPTQ without rotations — it isolates the rotation's contribution, which is central to claiming the method "generalizes." But if the question is strictly RTN-vs-GPTQ *within* QuaRot, dropping the plain baselines halves the run count. Please confirm scope.
- **(d) Compute budget:** I will assume 1× A100-80GB (or 2× A100-40GB) as the feasibility baseline: Phi-3-mini (~3.8B) fits easily in bf16. Rough estimate: QuaRot calibration + GPTQ ≈ 2–4 h per condition; RTN near-instant; lm-eval suite ≈ 0.5–1 h per condition. Total ≈ 2–4 GPU-days for all 19 conditions; well within a single-week allocation. CPU-only is infeasible for this scale. I'll flag this as an assumption, not a fixed requirement.
- **Other risks/uncertainties:** (i) whether the QuaRot repo supports the Phi-3 architecture out of the box (GQA/attention differences vs LLaMA) — likely minor model-adapter work, but a real implementation risk to call out; (ii) activation-bit policy per weight bit-width (W-only vs W+A) materially changes results and needs a decision before the full design; (iii) whether to include the LLaMA-2-7B port-validation control (adds ~1 day but de-risks the whole study); (iv) I'd like to consult your source-backed setup topics (calibration details, native bit-width support, evaluation set) before finalizing — the full design will pin these down.

I'll wait for your review/approval before producing the full design.
